plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Borrowed it. He was a knight, I am told.
plan.say: Borrowed it. He was a knight, I am told.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: That was never proved.
plan.say: That was never proved.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: The wind is pulling left.
plan.say: The wind is pulling left.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: He can stand at a gate. Ask me again when something comes to it.
plan.say: He can stand at a gate. Ask me again when something comes to it.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Has he sent yours?
plan.say: Has he sent yours?

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Then for once, Goda Malkin, we are on the same side of something. Sit down, I will stand you a cup.
plan.say: Then for once, Goda Malkin, we are on the same side of something. Sit down, I will stand you a cup.

plan.speaker: ivo
plan.text: Davy? He is fifteen.
plan.say: Davy? He is fifteen.

plan.speaker: ivo
plan.text: Tell him the boots are the easy part. It is the standing.
plan.say: Tell him the boots are the easy part. It is the standing.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Hold there, traveller. Brackenfell is a quiet place and I mean to keep it so. But you have the look of the road on you: tired, and honest enough. Greta at the Honeyed Hart keeps a bed for folk like you. Straight down this road to the square. It’s the tall house with the lantern.
plan.say: Hold there, traveller. Brackenfell is a quiet place and I mean to keep it so. But you have the look of the road on you: tired, and honest enough. Gretta at the Honeyed Hart keeps a bed for folk like you. Straight down this road to the square. It's the tall house with the lantern.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: You lit the harvest fire. I never thought to see it burn again. You’re one of us now, whether you like it or not.
plan.say: You lit the harvest fire. I never thought to see it burn again. You're one of us now, whether you like it or not.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Road’s quiet. Just how I like it.
plan.say: Road's quiet. Just how I like it.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: The old watchtower, up the crag to the north-east. It held a beacon once. Burned out before my grandfather’s day. Children dare each other up there, though they swear to me they don’t.
plan.say: The old watchtower, up the crag to the north-east. It held a beacon once. Burned out before my grandfather's day. Children dare each other up there, though they swear to me they don't.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Last village before the Greyspine passes. Sixty souls, one inn, one forge, and a chapel bell that no longer rings. Mind the river. The Stonewater is colder than she looks, and she doesn’t give back what she takes.
plan.say: Last village before the Greyspine passes. Sixty souls, one inn, one forge, and a chapel bell that no longer rings. Mind the river. The Stonewater is colder than she looks, and she doesn't give back what she takes.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Well now, a new face! Hale sent you? Then you’re welcome under this roof. There’s a bed up the stairs, by the window. It’s yours while you stay. But I’ll ask a kindness in return. Osric at the mill owes me a sack of malt, and I can’t brew on promises. Fetch it for me?
plan.say: Well now, a new face! Hale sent you? Then you're welcome under this roof. There's a bed up the stairs, by the window. It's yours while you stay. But I'll ask a kindness in return. Osric at the mill owes me a sack of malt, and I can't brew on promises. Fetch it for me?

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: You’re a treasure. Over the bridge east of the square, then follow the river downstream. You’ll hear the wheel before you see it.
plan.say: You're a treasure. Over the bridge east of the square, then follow the river downstream. You'll hear the wheel before you see it.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The mill is over the bridge east of the square, then down the river. Osric will know what I’m owed.
plan.say: The mill is over the bridge east of the square, then down the river. Osric will know what I'm owed.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: That’s the malt! Oh, bless you. There’ll be ale by week’s end. Here, for your trouble, and a bottle of the last batch.
plan.say: That's the malt! Oh, bless you. There'll be ale by week's end. Here, for your trouble, and a bottle of the last batch.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: If you’ve a mind to stay useful: Brandt has been storming about since his hammer went missing, old Maren is short of frostcaps, and Brother Aldous frets over that silent bell of his. And the Elder likes company, out under the oak.
plan.say: If you've a mind to stay useful: Brant has been storming about since his hammer went missing, old Marren is short of frostcaps, and Brother Aldous frets over that silent bell of his. And the Elder likes company, out under the oak.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The whole village in my hall, and the fire lit in the square. I could weep. Sit, drink!
plan.say: The whole village in my hall, and the fire lit in the square. I could weep. Sit, drink!

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: What can I get you, love?
plan.say: What can I get you, love?

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: It’s two gold, love, and your purse is light. Help a few folk around the village and come back.
plan.say: It's two gold, love, and your purse is light. Help a few folk around the village and come back.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Warm, and sweet with heather honey. The room feels friendlier already.
plan.say: Warm, and sweet with heather honey. The room feels friendlier already.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Three generations of Barleybrooks have kept this hearth. The beams came down from the beacon forest, and the recipe for the ale came from my gran, who took it from a traveller in trade for a night’s lodging. So you see, I’ve a soft spot for strangers.
plan.say: Three generations of Barleybrooks have kept this hearth. The beams came down from the beacon forest, and the recipe for the ale came from my gran, who took it from a traveller in trade for a night's lodging. So you see, I've a soft spot for strangers.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Up the stairs at the back, the bed by the window. Sleep as late as you like.
plan.say: Up the stairs at the back, the bed by the window. Sleep as late as you like.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Do me one small favour first and there’s a bed in it for you.
plan.say: Do me one small favour first and there's a bed in it for you.

plan.speaker: osric
plan.text: Greta’s malt! I’d clean forgot, what with the wheel groaning all week. Here, take it, and tell her the next sack is on me. I’d carry it myself, but the stones won’t dress themselves.
plan.say: Gretta's malt! I'd clean forgot, what with the wheel groaning all week. Here, take it, and tell her the next sack is on me. I'd carry it myself, but the stones won't dress themselves.

plan.speaker: osric
plan.text: Mind the dust. A mill is no place for a naked flame, or a fool.
plan.say: Mind the dust. A mill is no place for a naked flame, or a fool.

plan.speaker: osric
plan.text: The Stonewater turns my wheel, the wheel turns the stones, and the stones feed the valley. Simple as bread. Listen: you can hear her running true.
plan.say: The Stonewater turns my wheel, the wheel turns the stones, and the stones feed the valley. Simple as bread. Listen: you can hear her running true.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Unless you’ve come to tell me where my hammer is, I’ve work to do. My best cross-peen, gone from the bench three days back. And that boy Tobin can’t look me in the eye.
plan.say: Unless you've come to tell me where my hammer is, I've work to do. My best cross-peen, gone from the bench three days back. And that boy Tobbin can't look me in the eye.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Hm. Start with the boy. He’s always underfoot in the square, when he should be at the bellows.
plan.say: Hm. Start with the boy. He's always underfoot in the square, when he should be at the bellows.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: That’s her! Where was she? The watchtower? I’ll tan his... no. No, I was a boy once, and that tower was a castle then too. Take this. I made it for no one in particular, and it seems that was you.
plan.say: That's her! Where was she? The watchtower? I'll tan his... no. No, I was a boy once, and that tower was a castle then too. Take this. I made it for no one in particular, and it seems that was you.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: She rings true again. Hear that? That’s the sound of a village with a working forge.
plan.say: She rings true again. Hear that? That's the sound of a village with a working forge.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Find the boy. Tobin. Fair hair, guilty face.
plan.say: Find the boy. Tobbin. Fair hair, guilty face.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: The watchtower, he said? Up the crag past the chapel. Mind your footing.
plan.say: The watchtower, he said? Up the crag past the chapel. Mind your footing.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Iron from the Greyspine, charcoal from the pine, water from the Stonewater. Everything in this valley was made within sight of it. That’s rarer than you’d think.
plan.say: Iron from the Greyspine, charcoal from the pine, water from the Stonewater. Everything in this valley was made within sight of it. That's rarer than you'd think.

plan.speaker: tobin
plan.text: The hammer? I, um. I only borrowed it! I was playing knights up at the old watchtower, and then it got dark, and I ran, and... I left it by the fire ring. Please don’t tell him it was me.
plan.say: The hammer? I, um. I only borrowed it! I was playing knights up at the old watchtower, and then it got dark, and I ran, and... I left it by the fire ring. Please don't tell him it was me.

plan.speaker: tobin
plan.text: He wasn’t even cross! Well. He was a bit cross.
plan.say: He wasn't even cross! Well. He was a bit cross.

plan.speaker: tobin
plan.text: Bet you can’t beat me to the well!
plan.say: Bet you can't beat me to the well!

plan.speaker: tobin
plan.text: A smith, like Brandt. I’m going to forge a sword as tall as Warden Hale. Taller!
plan.say: A smith, like Brant. I'm going to forge a sword as tall as Warden Hale. Taller!

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Hm. Young eyes. Good. The frost came early and my stores are thin. I need frostcaps: pale blue, and they glow a little at dusk. They grow where it is cold and quiet. By the lake, at the forest’s edge, near old stones. Bring me five.
plan.say: Hm. Young eyes. Good. The frost came early and my stores are thin. I need frostcaps: pale blue, and they glow a little at dusk. They grow where it is cold and quiet. By the lake, at the forest's edge, near old stones. Bring me five.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Five, and not one bruised! You have gentle hands. Take this tonic. It will keep the mountain chill from your bones.
plan.say: Five, and not one bruised! You have gentle hands. Take this tonic. It will keep the mountain chill from your bones.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Sixty winters in this valley. I have buried more secrets in that garden than turnips.
plan.say: Sixty winters in this valley. I have buried more secrets in that garden than turnips.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Fevers, mostly. And grief, a little, though I don’t tell them that’s what’s in the tea.
plan.say: Fevers, mostly. And grief, a little, though I don't tell them that's what's in the tea.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: The peace of the Dawn upon you. Forgive the quiet. Our bell rope rotted through at midsummer, and I have neither the coin nor the knees to replace it. A village without its bell is a body without a voice.
plan.say: The peace of the Dawn upon you. Forgive the quiet. Our bell rope rotted through at midsummer, and I have neither the coin nor the knees to replace it. A village without its bell is a body without a voice.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Would you? Marta keeps good hemp at her shop on the square. The Dawn remembers a kindness.
plan.say: Would you? Marta keeps good hemp at her shop on the square. The Dawn remembers a kindness.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Hemp, and well laid! Give me one moment in the tower... there. It is done. Would you ring it? It ought to be a friend who rings it first.
plan.say: Hemp, and well laid! Give me one moment in the tower... there. It is done. Would you ring it? It ought to be a friend who rings it first.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Marta keeps good hemp rope at her shop on the square, east side.
plan.say: Marta keeps good hemp rope at her shop on the square, east side.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: The rope hangs under the tower, by the door. Pull, and let the valley hear.
plan.say: The rope hangs under the tower, by the door. Pull, and let the valley hear.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Listen. The valley has its voice again.
plan.say: Listen. The valley has its voice again.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Only that the night ends. Every night, without fail. We find that worth a small stone house and a bell.
plan.say: Only that the night ends. Every night, without fail. We find that worth a small stone house and a bell.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Quill’s Sundries. If I don’t have it, you don’t need it.
plan.say: Quill's Sundries. If I don't have it, you don't need it.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Thirty feet of the best. Don’t hang anything you can’t lift.
plan.say: Thirty feet of the best. Don't hang anything you can't lift.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Baked this morning. Mostly.
plan.say: Baked this morning. Mostly.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: From Edda’s trees. Sweetest in the valley.
plan.say: From Edda's trees. Sweetest in the valley.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: I trade with the lowland caravans twice a year. The rest of the time I trade in gossip, and the price is always fair.
plan.say: I trade with the lowland caravans twice a year. The rest of the time I trade in gossip, and the price is always fair.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Brackenfell remembers its friends. Stay as long as you like. Stay for good, if the road will let you.
plan.say: Brackenfell remembers its friends. Stay as long as you like. Stay for good, if the road will let you.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: The inn has its ale, the forge its hammer, Maren her remedies, and the bell its voice. Do you know how long it has been since Brackenfell was whole? We used to light a fire in the square at harvest’s end, and the whole valley would come. Light it tonight. You have earned the tinder.
plan.say: The inn has its ale, the forge its hammer, Marren her remedies, and the bell its voice. Do you know how long it has been since Brackenfell was whole? We used to light a fire in the square at harvest's end, and the whole valley would come. Light it tonight. You have earned the tinder.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Sit a while. An old man’s stories are all the entertainment this square can afford.
plan.say: Sit a while. An old man's stories are all the entertainment this square can afford.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Before the bell there was the beacon on the crag, and before the beacon, only the stars. We have always found some way to say: here we are. Come and find us.
plan.say: Before the bell there was the beacon on the crag, and before the beacon, only the stars. We have always found some way to say: here we are. Come and find us.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Begin with Greta at the inn. Everything in Brackenfell begins there.
plan.say: Begin with Gretta at the inn. Everything in Brackenfell begins there.

plan.speaker: edda
plan.text: Wheat’s in, mostly. Chickens are out, always.
plan.say: Wheat's in, mostly. Chickens are out, always.

plan.speaker: edda
plan.text: Fairweather land, five generations. The soil is thin and the summers short, but the bread tastes of it. If you see Bram dawdling at the market, tell him the barn won’t sweep itself.
plan.say: Fairweather land, five generations. The soil is thin and the summers short, but the bread tastes of it. If you see Bram dawdling at the market, tell him the barn won't sweep itself.

plan.speaker: finn
plan.text: Shh. You’ll scare the char.
plan.say: Shh. You'll scare the char.

plan.speaker: finn
plan.text: Mirrormere gives what she gives. She’s deep in the middle, mind. Deeper than the watchtower is tall, they say. Oh, and there’s one of Maren’s blue flowers on the shore yonder, if you’re collecting.
plan.say: Mirror meer gives what she gives. She's deep in the middle, mind. Deeper than the watchtower is tall, they say. Oh, and there's one of Marren's blue flowers on the shore yonder, if you're collecting.

plan.speaker: lark
plan.text: A song for the traveller? I know nine. Seven of them are sad.
plan.say: A song for the traveller? I know nine. Seven of them are sad.

plan.speaker: lark
plan.text: This one’s called “The Road Goes Ever Up.” It isn’t about anything. The good ones never are.
plan.say: This one's called "The Road Goes Ever Up." It isn't about anything. The good ones never are.

plan.speaker: lark
plan.text: I came for one night, two winters ago. Greta’s ale is a kind of gravity.
plan.say: I came for one night, two winters ago. Gretta's ale is a kind of gravity.

plan.speaker: wren
plan.text: You walk loud.
plan.say: You walk loud.

plan.speaker: wren
plan.text: Forest edge, north-west of the gate. Another on the rocks above the river, north of the bridge. And one past my cabin, where the ground stays cold. Don’t trample them.
plan.say: Forest edge, north-west of the gate. Another on the rocks above the river, north of the bridge. And one past my cabin, where the ground stays cold. Don't trample them.

plan.speaker: wren
plan.text: Hare. Grouse. Silence, mostly.
plan.say: Hare. Grouse. Silence, mostly.

plan.speaker: pip
plan.text: Have you seen a chicken? Not for any reason.
plan.say: Have you seen a chicken? Not for any reason.

plan.speaker: pip
plan.text: My mum sells cloth and says I have to stay where she can see me. So I’m going to be a knight. Or a chicken farmer. I haven’t decided.
plan.say: My mum sells cloth and says I have to stay where she can see me. So I'm going to be a knight. Or a chicken farmer. I haven't decided.

plan.speaker: ivo
plan.text: Patrol’s quiet. Keep to the roads after dark, friend.
plan.say: Patrol's quiet. Keep to the roads after dark, friend.

plan.speaker: ivo
plan.text: Stonewater Bridge? Older than the village. Older than the chapel. Whoever built it meant for something to be on the other side.
plan.say: Stonewater Bridge? Older than the village. Older than the chapel. Whoever built it meant for something to be on the other side.

plan.speaker: hilda
plan.text: Wool from the high pastures, dyed with Maren’s roots. Feel that. Go on.
plan.say: Wool from the high pastures, dyed with Marren's roots. Feel that. Go on.

plan.speaker: hilda
plan.text: It keeps us fed. And if my Pip offers to sell you a chicken, it isn’t hers.
plan.say: It keeps us fed. And if my Pip offers to sell you a chicken, it isn't hers.

plan.speaker: bram
plan.text: Apples! Cabbages! Oh. Sorry. Habit.
plan.say: Apples! Cabbages! Oh. Sorry. Habit.

plan.speaker: bram
plan.text: Not a coin? Go on, then. Don’t tell Edda.
plan.say: Not a coin? Go on, then. Don't tell Edda.

plan.speaker: bram
plan.text: Best in the valley. Only in the valley, mind, but still.
plan.say: Best in the valley. Only in the valley, mind, but still.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Safer than most. But there has been smoke in the pines north-west of the gate these three nights, and it is not Wren’s. Outlaws, come down off the passes before the snow. Hale cannot leave the gate, and I am too old to do more than worry. If you carry a blade and know its use, drive them off. Mind the big one.
plan.say: Safer than most. But there has been smoke in the pines north-west of the gate these three nights, and it is not Wren's. Outlaws, come down off the passes before the snow. Hale cannot leave the gate, and I am too old to do more than worry. If you carry a blade and know its use, drive them off. Mind the big one.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: North-west of the gate, among the pines. You will see their rag on a pole before they see you, if you are careful. Eat before you go, and do not be too proud to run.
plan.say: North-west of the gate, among the pines. You will see their rag on a pole before they see you, if you are careful. Eat before you go, and do not be too proud to run.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Then the children can pick berries at the wood’s edge again. This was my father’s, and it has hung on the wall long enough. Take it, with the village’s thanks.
plan.say: Then the children can pick berries at the wood's edge again. This was my father's, and it has hung on the wall long enough. Take it, with the village's thanks.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Troubled me? They had my second-best tongs and a roll of files off the cart at the ford, a week gone. Their chief wears them on his belt like trophies. One ear, red beard. They camp west of the path up to the old watchtower. Bring my tools back and I’ll put a proper sword in your hand, not that kitchen iron.
plan.say: Troubled me? They had my second-best tongs and a roll of files off the cart at the ford, a week gone. Their chief wears them on his belt like trophies. One ear, red beard. They camp west of the path up to the old watchtower. Bring my tools back and I'll put a proper sword in your hand, not that kitchen iron.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Hah! Not a scratch on them. As promised: an arming sword, drawn out this spring and waiting for a hand. Keep the point low and your feet moving.
plan.say: Hah! Not a scratch on them. As promised: an arming sword, drawn out this spring and waiting for a hand. Keep the point low and your feet moving.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: There’s coin on the board for outlaws, and I’ll pay it myself. Five of them put down and the road is a road again. Two camps: one in the pines north-west of here, one under the old watchtower. Don’t take on more than you can see.
plan.say: There's coin on the board for outlaws, and I'll pay it myself. Five of them put down and the road is a road again. Two camps: one in the pines north-west of here, one under the old watchtower. Don't take on more than you can see.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Five, by my count and yours. Paid in full. You’ve done the valley a turn, and I’ll not forget it.
plan.say: Five, by my count and yours. Paid in full. You've done the valley a turn, and I'll not forget it.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Twenty-four, child. Frostcaps do not pick themselves.
plan.say: Twenty-four, child. Frostcaps do not pick themselves.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Drink it when you bleed, not before. It is no use against foolishness.
plan.say: Drink it when you bleed, not before. It is no use against foolishness.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Since you are the sort who walks: I have a tea I used to make from three herbs and my knees now refuse. Bogbean from the hermit’s pool, sunwort from the bee meadow, stonecrop from the old stones on the eastern hill. It is the only thing that lets Edda’s widow sleep.
plan.say: Since you are the sort who walks: I have a tea I used to make from three herbs and my knees now refuse. Bogbean from the hermit's pool, sunwort from the bee meadow, stonecrop from the old stones on the eastern hill. It is the only thing that lets Edda's widow sleep.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: All three. And the stonecrop still wet. Sit, sit. I will brew it now, and you shall have the first cup.
plan.say: All three. And the stonecrop still wet. Sit, sit. I will brew it now, and you shall have the first cup.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Where did you… that is Corwin’s cap. Hob’s brother went down the old mine after silver, a good while back. So. It is the end of a long hope. Thank you for bringing it home rather than leaving it to the damp.
plan.say: Where did you... that is Corwin's cap. Hob's brother went down the old mine after silver, a good while back. So. It is the end of a long hope. Thank you for bringing it home rather than leaving it to the damp.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Corwin the miner. He went into the old workings north-west of here, up under the cliffs past the chapel, after silver; his brother Hob was the last to see him. The Warden barred the door afterwards. If you come across anything of his, I would be glad of it.
plan.say: Corwin the miner. He went into the old workings north-west of here, up under the cliffs past the chapel, after silver; his brother Hob was the last to see him. The Warden barred the door afterwards. If you come across anything of his, I would be glad of it.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Finn pulled a man out of the lake at first light. He’s on a bier at the wharf, south end of the town. Go and look, if you’ve the stomach, before the gossips make a story of him.
plan.say: Finn pulled a man out of the lake at first light. He's on a bier at the wharf, south end of the town. Go and look, if you've the stomach, before the gossips make a story of him.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text:
That’s Corwin’s hand. Alive, then, or he was. Let me see.

Bread. Fifty years of bread, in a cave on the shore. I barred that door and told myself it was to keep them out.
plan.say: That's Corwin's hand. Alive, then, or he was. Let me see. Bread. Fifty years of bread, in a cave on the shore. I barred that door and told myself it was to keep them out.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: That something went wrong below, before I wore this helmet. That Rowan went out to the shore every dawn and never said why. I didn’t ask. A man can keep a gate for thirty years that way.
plan.say: That something went wrong below, before I wore this helmet. That Rowan went out to the shore every dawn and never said why. I didn't ask. A man can keep a gate for thirty years that way.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Not here. Rowan knows the way to the lake cave; he’s walked it with a pail more mornings than I’ve slept. Go and ask him, and don’t let him tell you it’s nothing.
plan.say: Not here. Rowan knows the way to the lake cave; he's walked it with a pail more mornings than I've slept. Go and ask him, and don't let him tell you it's nothing.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Brass, and a number. OM fourteen: the Old Mine, Dunstan Pell. He dug under Corwin, a good while back.
plan.say: Brass, and a number. OM fourteen: the Old Mine, Dunstan Pell. He dug under Corwin, a good while back.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: No. Dry as a bone inside and thin as a rake: he walked a long way on nothing, in the dark. That’s no lake’s work.
plan.say: No. Dry as a bone inside and thin as a rake: he walked a long way on nothing, in the dark. That's no lake's work.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: The door in the north-west cliffs, up past the chapel. Hale barred it, but the Sexton kept the key, and old Sextons keep everything. Look in the crypt under the chapel.
plan.say: The door in the north-west cliffs, up past the chapel. Hale barred it, but the Sexton kept the key, and old Sextons keep everything. Look in the crypt under the chapel.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: There’s a vestment chest in the sacristy that I’ve never had the heart to open. The Sexton’s things are in it. The crypt gate under the nave has a lock to match.

plan.speaker: finn
plan.text: First light, face down in the reeds. The lake gives drowned men back swollen. This one was thin as a rake and dry as kindling. Whatever he was, he walked to the water; he didn’t fall in.

plan.speaker: pip
plan.text: A man under a sheet! Hale said not to look. I looked. He’s got silver in his teeth.
plan.say: A man under a sheet! Hale said not to look. I looked. He's got silver in his teeth.

plan.speaker: pip
plan.text: There’s a trunk up on the Hart’s roof walk. I climbed up. It’s locked, and Greta says it isn’t hers, but she looked cross.
plan.say: There's a trunk up on the Hart's roof walk. I climbed up. It's locked, and Gretta says it isn't hers, but she looked cross.

plan.speaker: pip
plan.text: There’s lights behind the chapel after midnight. Two people. I’m not allowed out, so I didn’t see them.
plan.say: There's lights behind the chapel after midnight. Two people. I'm not allowed out, so I didn't see them.

plan.speaker: pip
plan.text: Nothing. I’m being good today.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: You’ve one already, dear. Don’t be greedy with light.
plan.say: You've one already, dear. Don't be greedy with light.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Fill it before you go and mind the oil. Where you’re going, you’ll want it.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text:
Sit down, you’re making me tired. ... Hale has read it, then. I thought he might. I thought it would be me they came for one day.

The cave on the lake shore. The cellar of the Hart. I’ll tell you the rest, but not on my feet, and not today.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Tomorrow, I said. An old man needs a night to find the words. Sleep, and come back.
plan.say: Tomorrow, I said. An old man needs a night to find the words. Sleep, and come back.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Hold there, traveller. No, sit, I am off the gate till morning. Brackenfell is a quiet place and I mean to keep it so. But you have the look of the road on you: tired, and honest enough. Greta keeps a bed for folk like you. That is her, behind the bar.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Good. That’s the end of it. This time.
plan.say: Good. That's the end of it. This time.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: You haven’t the coin. Then it’s the cell. Come on.
plan.say: You haven't the coin. Then it's the cell. Come on.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Paid. Keep your hands in your pockets in future.
plan.say: Paid. Keep your hands in your pockets in future.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: There’s no cell to hold you. Go on, then.
plan.say: There's no cell to hold you. Go on, then.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Eat it while it’s hot. I don’t do cold.
plan.say: Eat it while it's hot. I don't do cold.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Three gold, love. Your purse says otherwise.
plan.say: Three gold, love. Your purse says otherwise.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Four gold, love, and I’ll not haggle with a purse that light.
plan.say: Four gold, love, and I'll not haggle with a purse that light.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Up the stairs, the bed by the window. Sleep till you’re done.
plan.say: Up the stairs, the bed by the window. Sleep till you're done.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: That’s a fine blade. Don’t draw it in my square.
plan.say: That's a fine blade. Don't draw it in my square.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Good. It sits well in your hand. My work.
plan.say: Good. It sits well in your hand. My work.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Where did you get that? Those are my grandfather’s dies, fifty years back. Old Mine steel.
plan.say: Where did you get that? Those are my grandfather's dies, fifty years back. Old Mine steel.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: You’re bleeding on my floor. Sit.
plan.say: You're bleeding on my floor. Sit.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Off down a hole, love? I’ll keep the bed made.
plan.say: Off down a hole, love? I'll keep the bed made.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Odd thing to carry. I’ll not ask.
plan.say: Odd thing to carry. I'll not ask.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: The Dawn keep you. You look as though you have seen the dead.
plan.say: The Dawn keep you. You look as though you have seen the dead.

plan.speaker: finn
plan.text: Still thinking about that man, aren’t you. So am I.
plan.say: Still thinking about that man, aren't you. So am I.

plan.speaker: ivo
plan.text: A lantern by day. Either you’re lost, or you’re going somewhere I’d not.
plan.say: A lantern by day. Either you're lost, or you're going somewhere I'd not.

plan.speaker: ivo
plan.text: Good. That’s the end of it. This time.

plan.text: You haven’t the coin. Then it’s the cell. Come on.

plan.text: Paid. Keep your hands in your pockets in future.

plan.speaker: ivo
plan.text: There’s no cell to hold you. Go on, then.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Three weeks now without the bread. They will be counting.
plan.say: Three weeks now without the bread. They will be counting.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: There is a stranger in town. Strangers ask about barred doors.
plan.say: There is a stranger in town. Strangers ask about barred doors.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Then Hale is closer than I would like. Say nothing in the Hart.
plan.say: Then Hale is closer than I would like. Say nothing in the Hart.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: And if they go down?
plan.say: And if they go down?

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Then they find what Corwin found. Go, before the watch comes round.
plan.say: Then they find what Corwin found. Go, before the watch comes round.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The house on the south lane? Nobody’s lived there in years. Pass the salt, love, and don’t ask me twice.
plan.say: The house on the south lane? Nobody's lived there in years. Pass the salt, love, and don't ask me twice.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Oh, that. I sell nothing to that house and I take nothing from it. Will you be wanting candles?
plan.say: Oh, that. I sell nothing to that house and I take nothing from it. Will you be wanting candles?

plan.speaker: finn
plan.text: Don’t look at the shutters. My father said never to look at the shutters.
plan.say: Don't look at the shutters. My father said never to look at the shutters.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: There are houses the Dawn will not name, child. That is one. Leave it to her.
plan.say: There are houses the Dawn will not name, child. That is one. Leave it to her.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Sound work, that. Look after it and it will look after you.
plan.say: Sound work, that. Look after it and it will look after you.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Iron from the Greyspine, every piece. I don’t haggle.
plan.say: Iron from the Greyspine, every piece. I don't haggle.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Let’s see it, then.
plan.say: Let's see it, then.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: You’ve nothing I’d give coin for. Outlaws carry better than they deserve, mind.
plan.say: You've nothing I'd give coin for. Outlaws carry better than they deserve, mind.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Not while the watch is asking after you. Square it with the Warden, then we’ll talk iron.
plan.say: Not while the watch is asking after you. Square it with the Warden, then we'll talk iron.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Not today, dear. Hale has been asking after you, and I’ll not buy from a name he is asking after.
plan.say: Not today, dear. Hale has been asking after you, and I'll not buy from a name he is asking after.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Not while the watch is asking after you. I’ve a name to keep.
plan.say: Not while the watch is asking after you. I've a name to keep.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Let’s have a look, dear.
plan.say: Let's have a look, dear.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Whale oil. It stinks and it burns. Don’t spill it near the candles.
plan.say: Whale oil. It stinks and it burns. Don't spill it near the candles.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Grey silver, never stamped. Aye, I can. Three bars and ninety gold, and the edge will outlast the blade. Mind, I’ll want to know where you had it.
plan.say: Grey silver, never stamped. Aye, I can. Three bars and ninety gold, and the edge will outlast the blade. Mind, I'll want to know where you had it.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Done. Don’t draw it in the Hart.
plan.say: Done. Don't draw it in the Hart.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: They say Tobin’s been up the Watch Bell more than the Watch has. A tin box, a lockpick, and a boy who will not say what he saw from the top.
plan.say: They say Tobbin's been up the Watch Bell more than the Watch has. A tin box, a lockpick, and a boy who will not say what he saw from the top.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: There’s a stone in the terrace wall below the Elder’s plaque with crooked mortar. Folk have stopped noticing it. The Magpie never did.
plan.say: There's a stone in the terrace wall below the Elder's plaque with crooked mortar. Folk have stopped noticing it. The Magpie never did.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The Magpie keeps a cellar on Washing Lane, under a hatch no bigger than a cheese-board. Keeps the key somewhere sillier than a pocket.
plan.say: The Magpie keeps a cellar on Washing Lane, under a hatch no bigger than a cheese-board. Keeps the key somewhere sillier than a pocket.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The old Elder had a strongbox put in the quay when the Wharf was built. Reached from the water. I never knew a man who had the key.
plan.say: The old Elder had a strongbox put in the quay when the Wharf was built. Reached from the water. I never knew a man who had the key.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The Magpie walks at dusk from the square to somewhere west of the weavers, same road each time. Nobody follows her. You’d have to be patient.
plan.say: The Magpie walks at dusk from the square to somewhere west of the weavers, same road each time. Nobody follows her. You'd have to be patient.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The shut house on the south lane. Don’t ask Marta. Don’t ask Finn. Ask nobody. Take a key, if you’ve one with a wren on it.
plan.say: The shut house on the south lane. Don't ask Marta. Don't ask Finn. Ask nobody. Take a key, if you've one with a wren on it.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The mine door has been barred for fifty years. The Sexton kept the key, and old Sextons keep everything.
plan.say: The mine door has been barred for fifty years. The Sexton kept the key, and old Sextons keep everything.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: My grandmother said the Old Mine’s foreman kept a strongbox below and wore the key round his neck. Nobody has been down to ask him.
plan.say: My grandmother said the Old Mine's foreman kept a strongbox below and wore the key round his neck. Nobody has been down to ask him.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: A drowned man on the wharf, dry as bone. The wise folk are keeping their windows shut.
plan.say: A drowned man on the wharf, dry as bone. The wise folk are keeping their windows shut.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Hale cries on the last day of the month. Pip told me. Pip tells everybody.
plan.say: Hale cries on the last day of the month. Pip told me. Pip tells everybody.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The Elder talks to the lake. Always has. Says it answers.
plan.say: The Elder talks to the lake. Always has. Says it answers.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Nothing new, love. Same faces, same ale.
plan.say: Nothing new, love. Same faces, same ale.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: You’ve nothing I’d give coin for. Outlaws carry better than they deserve, mind.
plan.say: You've nothing I'd give coin for. Outlaws carry better than they deserve, mind.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text:
The bread goes out at dawn. I carry it myself, and I am too old to be told it is a kindness.

The count stays kept. Sit. It will not hurt you to be counted.
plan.say: The bread goes out at dawn. I carry it myself, and I am too old to be told it is a kindness. The count stays kept. Sit. It will not hurt you to be counted.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text:
It is quiet. I did not know quiet could be this loud.

They are asleep. Thank you. I could not have said the names. I tried.
plan.say: It is quiet. I did not know quiet could be this loud. They are asleep. Thank you. I could not have said the names. I tried.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text:
Sit. You will want it from the start, and you will not like where it starts.

Fifty years back my father sold the last seam of the Old Mine to a Crown assayer, and the silver was singing, and he would not share it. He sealed the adit with twelve of his own shift still below. They did not die as you or I do. They stayed. They kept digging.
plan.say: Sit. You will want it from the start, and you will not like where it starts. Fifty years back my father sold the last seam of the Old Mine to a Crown assayer, and the silver was singing, and he would not share it. He sealed the adit with twelve of his own shift still below. They did not die as you or I do. They stayed. They kept digging.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text:
It was never for their bellies. It was so that someone remembered them. Every dawn a loaf and a pail, left on the slab in the cave on the shore, and the count said aloud: one to twelve. As long as the count is kept they stay men. If it is not, the song takes what is left of the men in them, and they come up.

I carried it thirty years.

As long as the count is kept they stay men. If it is not, the song takes what is left of the men in them, and they come up. I carried it thirty years.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: I stopped it. Three weeks ago. Greta has found a buyer who pays double and wants the silver by the barrow, and I am old, and I thought: let it end with me. Pell walked out by the lake cave to ask why the bread had not come. You saw how far a man gets in daylight who has been so long under.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text:
Go the way Greta’s people ran the silver out. The Hart’s cellar has a wall that was never the end of the cellar: the fresh brick on the east side. A tunnel runs from there under the town to the lake cave.

The twelve stand by the slab. You will know what to do when you see them. I never did.

A tunnel runs from there under the town to the lake cave. The twelve stand by the slab. You will know what to do when you see them. I never did.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Go on. The Hart. The east cellar wall, newer brick than the rest. Take bread. Take a light. Take your courage in both hands, because it has been a long while since anyone went that way and meant well.
plan.say: Go on. The Hart. The east cellar wall, newer brick than the rest. Take bread. Take a light. Take your courage in both hands, because it has been a long while since anyone went that way and meant well.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: I’ll not charge you for the stew this once, love. Don’t make it a habit.
plan.say: I'll not charge you for the stew this once, love. Don't make it a habit.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The Hart’s never been so full. People want to be near other people, after.
plan.say: The Hart's never been so full. People want to be near other people, after.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: The count is kept and the gate is quiet. I’ll sleep tonight with the key out of my hand.
plan.say: The count is kept and the gate is quiet. I'll sleep tonight with the key out of my hand.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: I’ve left the old door unbarred. Nothing in it wants out now.
plan.say: I've left the old door unbarred. Nothing in it wants out now.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Silver for a blade? Aye, I’ll work it now. It’s only metal again.
plan.say: Silver for a blade? Aye, I'll work it now. It's only metal again.

plan.speaker: finn
plan.text: Nobody’s come out of the lake since. I check every morning.
plan.say: Nobody's come out of the lake since. I check every morning.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The cellar? Down the stair by the door, love, behind the rail. Take a candle, the steps are steep.
plan.say: The cellar? Down the stair by the door, love, behind the rail. Take a candle, the steps are steep.

plan.speaker: godwin
plan.text: If I look half asleep it is because I am. The bread is made while you are dreaming.
plan.say: If I look half asleep it is because I am. The bread is made while you are dreaming.

plan.speaker: godwin
plan.text: Godwin Hobb. My mother baked at that oven and her mother before. Osric grinds it, I bake it, you eat it. That is a town.
plan.say: Godwin Hobb. My mother baked at that oven and her mother before. Osric grinds it, I bake it, you eat it. That is a town.

plan.speaker: godwin
plan.text: The Elder had six loaves off me every morning, paid by the month. Three weeks back he stopped. Never said why.
plan.say: The Elder had six loaves off me every morning, paid by the month. Three weeks back he stopped. Never said why.

plan.speaker: godwin
plan.text: You want it warm, find my Tilly at the stall by the bridge road. You want it warmer, be here before the light.
plan.say: You want it warm, find my Tilly at the stall by the bridge road. You want it warmer, be here before the light.

plan.speaker: godwin
plan.text: Mind the rack.
plan.say: Mind the rack.

plan.speaker: godwin
plan.text: Fresh at first light. Not before, not after.
plan.say: Fresh at first light. Not before, not after.

plan.speaker: godwin
plan.text: The bell is back. Thirty years I have drawn the first batch on its stroke. These weeks I burned more than I sold.
plan.say: The bell is back. Thirty years I have drawn the first batch on its stroke. These weeks I burned more than I sold.

plan.speaker: godwin
plan.text: I am awake all night, friend. That is the trade. You picked the one house in Brackenfell to creep into.
plan.say: I am awake all night, friend. That is the trade. You picked the one house in Brackenfell to creep into.

plan.speaker: avice
plan.text: Come in out of the flour, or into it, there is no difference in this house.
plan.say: Come in out of the flour, or into it, there is no difference in this house.

plan.speaker: avice
plan.text: I am Avice. I married the baker for the warm kitchen and stayed for the same reason.
plan.say: I am Avice. I married the baker for the warm kitchen and stayed for the same reason.

plan.speaker: avice
plan.text: Greta takes two dozen rounds a day for the Hart and pays on the nail. If the whole town paid like Greta I would be a lady.
plan.say: Gretta takes two dozen rounds a day for the Hart and pays on the nail. If the whole town paid like Gretta I would be a lady.

plan.speaker: avice
plan.text: Osric was fretting about malt he owes the Hart. If you are walking to the mill you would do him a kindness to ask.
plan.say: Osric was fretting about malt he owes the Hart. If you are walking to the mill you would do him a kindness to ask.

plan.speaker: avice
plan.text: Mind the step, it is slick with flour.
plan.say: Mind the step, it is slick with flour.

plan.speaker: avice
plan.text: Tilly! The stall!
plan.say: Tilly! The stall!

plan.speaker: avice
plan.text: Hester Slate saw them carry him up. She said he weighed nothing. She has lifted enough to know.
plan.say: Hester Slate saw them carry him up. She said he weighed nothing. She has lifted enough to know.

plan.speaker: avice
plan.text: Godwin! There is someone in the house! ... He is at the oven with a peel in his hand. I would go.
plan.say: Godwin! There is someone in the house! ... He is at the oven with a peel in his hand. I would go.

plan.speaker: tilly
plan.text: Rounds, long loaves, and honey cake if Tamsin brought the honey. She did. So, honey cake.
plan.say: Rounds, long loaves, and honey cake if Tamsin brought the honey. She did. So, honey cake.

plan.speaker: tilly
plan.text: Tilly Hobb. I sell what my father bakes and I count better than he does.
plan.say: Tilly Hobb. I sell what my father bakes and I count better than he does.

plan.speaker: tilly
plan.text: Giles Varrow walks the long way round to pass this stall. You can smell him coming. I do not mind it as much as I ought.
plan.say: Giles Varrow walks the long way round to pass this stall. You can smell him coming. I do not mind it as much as I ought.

plan.speaker: tilly
plan.text: The tinker down the row hears everything. If something is going on in this town, Diggory knew yesterday.
plan.say: The tinker down the row hears everything. If something is going on in this town, Diggory knew yesterday.

plan.speaker: tilly
plan.text: Honey cake! Last ones!
plan.say: Honey cake! Last ones!

plan.speaker: tilly
plan.text: Warm bread, warm bread.
plan.say: Warm bread, warm bread.

plan.speaker: tilly
plan.text: Father is himself again now the bell rings. Three weeks of burnt crusts, we had.
plan.say: Father is himself again now the bell rings. Three weeks of burnt crusts, we had.

plan.speaker: tilly
plan.text: I am calling my father, and he is holding something hot.
plan.say: I am calling my father, and he is holding something hot.

plan.speaker: idony
plan.text: Sit, if you are stopping. I am too old to look up at people.
plan.say: Sit, if you are stopping. I am too old to look up at people.

plan.speaker: idony
plan.text: Idony Hobb. I have buried a husband, two hens I was fond of, and most of the people who knew me as a girl.
plan.say: Idony Hobb. I have buried a husband, two hens I was fond of, and most of the people who knew me as a girl.

plan.speaker: idony
plan.text: Rowan was a boy with scabbed knees when they shut that hill. He has been an old man about it ever since.
plan.say: Rowan was a boy with scabbed knees when they shut that hill. He has been an old man about it ever since.

plan.speaker: idony
plan.text: If you want to know what this town keeps under its tongue, ask who the bread was for. Not me. Ask Rowan.
plan.say: If you want to know what this town keeps under its tongue, ask who the bread was for. Not me. Ask Rowan.

plan.speaker: idony
plan.text: Mind my hens.
plan.say: Mind my hens.

plan.speaker: idony
plan.text: Bell’s late. No. Bell’s not.
plan.say: Bell's late. No. Bell's not.

plan.speaker: idony
plan.text: So one of them walked out. I wondered who would live to see it. I did not want it to be me.
plan.say: So one of them walked out. I wondered who would live to see it. I did not want it to be me.

plan.speaker: idony
plan.text: At my age you are not frightening. You are only rude. Go home.
plan.say: At my age you are not frightening. You are only rude. Go home.

plan.speaker: hugh
plan.text: Draw arm. Show me. Hm. You pull with your shoulder. Everyone does until someone tells them.
plan.say: Draw arm. Show me. Hm. You pull with your shoulder. Everyone does until someone tells them.

plan.speaker: hugh
plan.text: Hugh Alder, fletcher. Shaft, feather and head, and I can tell you which goose the feather came from.
plan.say: Hugh Alder, fletcher. Shaft, feather and head, and I can tell you which goose the feather came from.

plan.speaker: hugh
plan.text: Hale and I have shot at the butts every seventh day since we were lads. He is still the better shot and still pretends otherwise.
plan.say: Hale and I have shot at the butts every seventh day since we were lads. He is still the better shot and still pretends otherwise.

plan.speaker: hugh
plan.text: Wren takes my broadheads by the dozen. Her cabin is west of the town; if you hunt, she is the one to ask.
plan.say: Wren takes my broadheads by the dozen. Her cabin is west of the town; if you hunt, she is the one to ask.

plan.speaker: hugh
plan.text: Straight grain. Always straight grain.
plan.say: Straight grain. Always straight grain.

plan.speaker: hugh
plan.text: Morning. How is the wind?
plan.say: Morning. How is the wind?

plan.speaker: hugh
plan.text: Hale asked me for two sheaves of arrows the day they found him. He has not ordered two in ten years.
plan.say: Hale asked me for two sheaves of arrows the day they found him. He has not ordered two in ten years.

plan.speaker: hugh
plan.text: There are four hundred arrows in this house and I made every one. Leave by the door you came in.
plan.say: There are four hundred arrows in this house and I made every one. Leave by the door you came in.

plan.speaker: gillian
plan.text: Take a seat and a feather. If you are talking to me you can strip quills while you do it.
plan.say: Take a seat and a feather. If you are talking to me you can strip quills while you do it.

plan.speaker: gillian
plan.text: Gillian Alder. I keep the house, I bind the fletchings, and I keep Hugh from giving arrows away to friends.
plan.say: Gillian Alder. I keep the house, I bind the fletchings, and I keep Hugh from giving arrows away to friends.

plan.speaker: gillian
plan.text: Our Stephen has the cobbler’s shop and sleeps over it, alone, eating who knows what. It is forty paces. I count them.
plan.say: Our Stephen has the cobbler's shop and sleeps over it, alone, eating who knows what. It is forty paces. I count them.

plan.speaker: gillian
plan.text: Edda at Fairweather Farm saves me her goose feathers. It is east over the bridge, past the mill. Mind her geese.
plan.say: Edda at Fairweather Farm saves me her goose feathers. It is east over the bridge, past the mill. Mind her geese.

plan.speaker: gillian
plan.text: Wipe your feet.
plan.say: Wipe your feet.

plan.speaker: gillian
plan.text: Is that Stephen? No.
plan.say: Is that Stephen? No.

plan.speaker: gillian
plan.text: Hugh says it is all finished now, one way or the other. Men say that. I have left the lamp trimmed.
plan.say: Hugh says it is all finished now, one way or the other. Men say that. I have left the lamp trimmed.

plan.speaker: gillian
plan.text: Hugh. Hugh! Wake up, there is someone, and you have a bow on the wall.
plan.say: Hugh. Hugh! Wake up, there is someone, and you have a bow on the wall.

plan.speaker: laurence
plan.text: A cask is thirty staves that hate each other, held by two hoops. That is all there is to know. It takes seven years to learn.
plan.say: A cask is thirty staves that hate each other, held by two hoops. That is all there is to know. It takes seven years to learn.

plan.speaker: laurence
plan.text: Laurence Byrd, cooper. The Hart’s ale, Goda’s beer, the salt fish: all in my oak.
plan.say: Laurence Byrd, cooper. The Hart's ale, Goda's beer, the salt fish: all in my oak.

plan.speaker: laurence
plan.text: My brother Randal builds boats on a lake with four boats on it. He had the hands to be a cooper.
plan.say: My brother Randal builds boats on a lake with four boats on it. He had the hands to be a cooper.

plan.speaker: laurence
plan.text: Greta is waiting on malt from the mill before she can fill what I made her. Osric forgets. Somebody should jog him.
plan.say: Gretta is waiting on malt from the mill before she can fill what I made her. Osric forgets. Somebody should jog him.

plan.speaker: laurence
plan.text: Tight as a drum.
plan.say: Tight as a drum.

plan.speaker: laurence
plan.text: Joyce! Hoops!
plan.say: Joyce! Hoops!

plan.speaker: laurence
plan.text: Greta wanted a cask moved in her cellar the week before they found him. Then she did not. I thought it odd then.
plan.say: Gretta wanted a cask moved in her cellar the week before they found him. Then she did not. I thought it odd then.

plan.speaker: laurence
plan.text: Joyce, the adze. No, the big one. Now, friend, which way is out? Show me.
plan.say: Joyce, the adze. No, the big one. Now, friend, which way is out? Show me.

plan.speaker: felice
plan.text: Come in. Mind the shavings. I would say I sweep them but nobody has ever caught up with a cooper.
plan.say: Come in. Mind the shavings. I would say I sweep them but nobody has ever caught up with a cooper.

plan.speaker: felice
plan.text: Felice Byrd. I shave hoops and keep the peace between a cooper and his daughter, which is the harder craft.
plan.say: Felice Byrd. I shave hoops and keep the peace between a cooper and his daughter, which is the harder craft.

plan.speaker: felice
plan.text: Maren cured my hands when I could not hold a knife. People call her sour. I call her the reason I can work.
plan.say: Marren cured my hands when I could not hold a knife. People call her sour. I call her the reason I can work.

plan.speaker: felice
plan.text: Old Maren has more than tonics in that cottage. She read the dead man’s tally when nobody else could. If you find a thing you cannot read, there is your door.
plan.say: Old Marren has more than tonics in that cottage. She read the dead man's tally when nobody else could. If you find a thing you cannot read, there is your door.

plan.speaker: felice
plan.text: Mind the shavings.
plan.say: Mind the shavings.

plan.speaker: felice
plan.text: Lovely morning for it.
plan.say: Lovely morning for it.

plan.speaker: felice
plan.text: I cried when I heard it. Silly. You do not know a thing holds your day together until it stops.
plan.say: I cried when I heard it. Silly. You do not know a thing holds your day together until it stops.

plan.speaker: felice
plan.text: Laurence! ... You have picked a house where everyone owns a blade with a handle at each end.
plan.say: Laurence! ... You have picked a house where everyone owns a blade with a handle at each end.

plan.speaker: joyce
plan.text: That one is mine. Raised it, hooped it, tight first time. Father will tell you he helped.
plan.say: That one is mine. Raised it, hooped it, tight first time. Father will tell you he helped.

plan.speaker: joyce
plan.text: Joyce Byrd. I have done seven years at the block the same as any apprentice. I want "and Daughter" on the board.
plan.say: Joyce Byrd. I have done seven years at the block the same as any apprentice. I want "and Daughter" on the board.

plan.speaker: joyce
plan.text: Old Wenn at the boatyard says a woman built the best boat that was ever on Mirrormere. He will not say who. I think it was his wife.
plan.say: Old Wenn at the boatyard says a woman built the best boat that was ever on Mirror meer. He will not say who. I think it was his wife.

plan.speaker: joyce
plan.text: The doors under the quay are the boat-houses, and Old Wenn has the keys. He will tell you a whole story before he tells you no.
plan.say: The doors under the quay are the boat-houses, and Old Wenn has the keys. He will tell you a whole story before he tells you no.

plan.speaker: joyce
plan.text: And Daughter. You will see.
plan.say: And Daughter. You will see.

plan.speaker: joyce
plan.text: Tight first time.
plan.say: Tight first time.

plan.speaker: joyce
plan.text: Everything in this town has changed but the sign over our door. I am working on that too.
plan.say: Everything in this town has changed but the sign over our door. I am working on that too.

plan.speaker: joyce
plan.text: I can swing a cooper’s adze all day. I can certainly swing it once.
plan.say: I can swing a cooper's adze all day. I can certainly swing it once.

plan.speaker: anselm
plan.text: Feel that. No, with the back of your hand. That is Hilda’s weaving, and there is none better this side of the passes.
plan.say: Feel that. No, with the back of your hand. That is Hilda's weaving, and there is none better this side of the passes.

plan.speaker: anselm
plan.text: Lindqvist. My grandfather carried cloth over the Greyspine on his back. I carry it across a counter and call it progress.
plan.say: Lindqvist. My grandfather carried cloth over the Greyspine on his back. I carry it across a counter and call it progress.

plan.speaker: anselm
plan.text: Brandt Ironhand wears a shirt of my cloth that he has not paid Hilda for. I notice it every time he lifts his arm.
plan.say: Brant Ironhand wears a shirt of my cloth that he has not paid Hilda for. I notice it every time he lifts his arm.

plan.speaker: anselm
plan.text: If you want honest work, read the board at the Hart. If you want a good coat, come back with silver.
plan.say: If you want honest work, read the board at the Hart. If you want a good coat, come back with silver.

plan.speaker: anselm
plan.text: Mind the bolts, they are not for leaning on.
plan.say: Mind the bolts, they are not for leaning on.

plan.speaker: anselm
plan.text: Good wool day. Dry.
plan.say: Good wool day. Dry.

plan.speaker: anselm
plan.text: You will have heard. I sold the sailcloth they laid over him. I would rather not have known what for.
plan.say: You will have heard. I sold the sailcloth they laid over him. I would rather not have known what for.

plan.speaker: anselm
plan.text: The shop is shut. Whatever you want will still be on the shelf in the morning, and so, I trust, will everything else.
plan.say: The shop is shut. Whatever you want will still be on the shelf in the morning, and so, I trust, will everything else.

plan.speaker: sabina
plan.text: Good day. Father will tell you the price is firm. It is not, but let him say it first.
plan.say: Good day. Father will tell you the price is firm. It is not, but let him say it first.

plan.speaker: sabina
plan.text: I keep the counter and the book. Father keeps the opinions.
plan.say: I keep the counter and the book. Father keeps the opinions.

plan.speaker: sabina
plan.text: Lark has owed me a song for two winters. I have decided it will be about me and it will be flattering.
plan.say: Lark has owed me a song for two winters. I have decided it will be about me and it will be flattering.

plan.speaker: sabina
plan.text: Brother Aldous was asking after rope for the bell. Marta Quill had hemp; the ropemaker is sore about it.
plan.say: Brother Aldous was asking after rope for the bell. Marta Quill had hemp; the ropemaker is sore about it.

plan.speaker: sabina
plan.text: That blue is Wilmot’s. Look at it.
plan.say: That blue is Wilmot's. Look at it.

plan.speaker: sabina
plan.text: Lark! Two winters!
plan.say: Lark! Two winters!

plan.speaker: sabina
plan.text: You are the one who got the bell ringing. I slept through the first one out of habit.
plan.say: You are the one who got the bell ringing. I slept through the first one out of habit.

plan.speaker: sabina
plan.text: We are closed, and I am in my nightgown, and you are leaving.
plan.say: We are closed, and I am in my nightgown, and you are leaving.

plan.speaker: petronel
plan.text: Hands. Let me see them. Hm. You work. Good, I do not sell to people who do not.
plan.say: Hands. Let me see them. Hm. You work. Good, I do not sell to people who do not.

plan.speaker: petronel
plan.text: Petronel Vey. I was a Lindqvist until I had the sense to marry out of drapery.
plan.say: Petronel Vey. I was a Lindqvist until I had the sense to marry out of drapery.

plan.speaker: petronel
plan.text: That apothecary, Mossop. Jars of coloured water and a long word for each. Maren has forgotten more than he has read.
plan.say: That apothecary, Mossop. Jars of coloured water and a long word for each. Marren has forgotten more than he has read.

plan.speaker: petronel
plan.text: Old Maren wants herbs gathered and her knees will not do it. Go and ask her. Say I sent you, she will be rude about it.
plan.say: Old Marren wants herbs gathered and her knees will not do it. Go and ask her. Say I sent you, she will be rude about it.

plan.speaker: petronel
plan.text: Gloves would hide those.
plan.say: Gloves would hide those.

plan.speaker: petronel
plan.text: Fulk’s skins are late again.
plan.say: Fulk's skins are late again.

plan.speaker: petronel
plan.text: A drowned man with dry lungs. I have skinned enough beasts to know that is not drowning.
plan.say: A drowned man with dry lungs. I have skinned enough beasts to know that is not drowning.

plan.speaker: petronel
plan.text: I sleep with my shears. Think about that, and then think about the door.
plan.say: I sleep with my shears. Think about that, and then think about the door.

plan.speaker: jocelyn
plan.text: Stand straight a moment. No, I am not selling you anything, I only cannot help measuring.
plan.say: Stand straight a moment. No, I am not selling you anything, I only cannot help measuring.

plan.speaker: jocelyn
plan.text: Jocelyn Lindqvist, tailor. My father sells the cloth and I cut it, and we argue about which is the harder.
plan.say: Jocelyn Lindqvist, tailor. My father sells the cloth and I cut it, and we argue about which is the harder.

plan.speaker: jocelyn
plan.text: Bridget Malkin laughed at something I said on Tuesday. I have been trying to remember what it was ever since.
plan.say: Bridget Malkin laughed at something I said on Tuesday. I have been trying to remember what it was ever since.

plan.speaker: jocelyn
plan.text: I cut the coats for the Highfold wedding. If you go up that way, see whether Kester Wold has split the seams yet.
plan.say: I cut the coats for the Highfold wedding. If you go up that way, see whether Kester Wold has split the seams yet.

plan.speaker: jocelyn
plan.text: That hem is a crime.
plan.say: That hem is a crime.

plan.speaker: jocelyn
plan.text: Morning. Shoulders back.
plan.say: Morning. Shoulders back.

plan.speaker: jocelyn
plan.text: They asked me to stitch the shroud. I have made wedding coats this month. I did not like the change.
plan.say: They asked me to stitch the shroud. I have made wedding coats this month. I did not like the change.

plan.speaker: jocelyn
plan.text: Out. I will not be robbed in a house full of pins by someone who cannot see them.
plan.say: Out. I will not be robbed in a house full of pins by someone who cannot see them.

plan.speaker: gilbert
plan.text: Thorne. If it comes over the passes or goes out by them, a little of it stays with me.
plan.say: Thorne. If it comes over the passes or goes out by them, a little of it stays with me.

plan.speaker: gilbert
plan.text: I buy what Brackenfell makes and sell it where they have never smelled a tannery. Somebody must.
plan.say: I buy what Brackenfell makes and sell it where they have never smelled a tannery. Somebody must.

plan.speaker: gilbert
plan.text: Hale would close the road for a fox. A warden who keeps everything out keeps trade out with it.
plan.say: Hale would close the road for a fox. A warden who keeps everything out keeps trade out with it.

plan.speaker: gilbert
plan.text: There is silver paid at the board for outlaws put down on the passes. I put some of that silver there myself.
plan.say: There is silver paid at the board for outlaws put down on the passes. I put some of that silver there myself.

plan.speaker: gilbert
plan.text: Time is money. Mostly mine.
plan.say: Time is money. Mostly mine.

plan.speaker: gilbert
plan.text: The passes, Hale! Think of the passes!
plan.say: The passes, Hale! Think of the passes!

plan.speaker: gilbert
plan.text: A dead stranger frightens caravans more than outlaws do. I want it explained, and I want it explained quietly.
plan.say: A dead stranger frightens caravans more than outlaws do. I want it explained, and I want it explained quietly.

plan.speaker: gilbert
plan.text: You are in a house with three locks and I heard every one. Sit down where I can see you while the watch is fetched.
plan.say: You are in a house with three locks and I heard every one. Sit down where I can see you while the watch is fetched.

plan.speaker: elinor
plan.text: Salt by the block, pepper by the pinch, and no, the pepper is not cheaper for asking twice.
plan.say: Salt by the block, pepper by the pinch, and no, the pepper is not cheaper for asking twice.

plan.speaker: elinor
plan.text: Elinor Thorne. Gilbert has the warehouse and the temper. I have the stall and the customers.
plan.say: Elinor Thorne. Gilbert has the warehouse and the temper. I have the stall and the customers.

plan.speaker: elinor
plan.text: Master Sele lends me books and I return them unread with a remark. He has never caught me. Lettice has.
plan.say: Master Sele lends me books and I return them unread with a remark. He has never caught me. Lettice has.

plan.speaker: elinor
plan.text: The scribe keeps school in the mornings and every old paper in the town. If it was written down, Emmet Sele has it.
plan.say: The scribe keeps school in the mornings and every old paper in the town. If it was written down, Emmet Sele has it.

plan.speaker: elinor
plan.text: Do not sneeze on the pepper.
plan.say: Do not sneeze on the pepper.

plan.speaker: elinor
plan.text: Fine salt, lake-dried.
plan.say: Fine salt, lake-dried.

plan.speaker: elinor
plan.text: The town talks of nothing else. I sell salt. People will still want salt.
plan.say: The town talks of nothing else. I sell salt. People will still want salt.

plan.speaker: elinor
plan.text: Gilbert. Gilbert! There is a person. No, do not fetch the ledger, fetch the poker.
plan.say: Gilbert. Gilbert! There is a person. No, do not fetch the ledger, fetch the poker.

plan.speaker: simon
plan.text: Onions, oats, lamp oil, lard. Edda’s cabbages when Bram remembers to bring them.
plan.say: Onions, oats, lamp oil, lard. Edda's cabbages when Bram remembers to bring them.

plan.speaker: simon
plan.text: Simon Thorne. The other Thorne. The one with the shop and the debts, not the house and the opinions.
plan.say: Simon Thorne. The other Thorne. The one with the shop and the debts, not the house and the opinions.

plan.speaker: simon
plan.text: My brother Gilbert owns the roof over this store, and reminds me on the first of every month.
plan.say: My brother Gilbert owns the roof over this store, and reminds me on the first of every month.

plan.speaker: simon
plan.text: Hale wants lamp oil for the gate. There is a notice for it on the board, and the oil is at Marta’s, not mine, more’s the pity.
plan.say: Hale wants lamp oil for the gate. There is a notice for it on the board, and the oil is at Marta's, not mine, more's the pity.

plan.speaker: simon
plan.text: Ned! Sacks!
plan.say: Ned! Sacks!

plan.speaker: simon
plan.text: Mind the lard.
plan.say: Mind the lard.

plan.speaker: simon
plan.text: I had a customer ask for something to keep the dead out. I sold him garlic. It does no harm.
plan.say: I had a customer ask for something to keep the dead out. I sold him garlic. It does no harm.

plan.speaker: simon
plan.text: There is nothing here worth a hanging. Oats. You would hang for oats?
plan.say: There is nothing here worth a hanging. Oats. You would hang for oats?

plan.speaker: ned
plan.text: I am not allowed to talk to strangers. Are you a stranger? You look like one.
plan.say: I am not allowed to talk to strangers. Are you a stranger? You look like one.

plan.speaker: ned
plan.text: Ned Thorne. I can carry a whole sack of oats. A small sack.
plan.say: Ned Thorne. I can carry a whole sack of oats. A small sack.

plan.speaker: ned
plan.text: Pip says she can climb the bell tower. She cannot. I cannot either, but I never said I could.
plan.say: Pip says she can climb the bell tower. She cannot. I cannot either, but I never said I could.

plan.speaker: ned
plan.text: There is a grey cat that sits on the rail of the hoist loft, behind the forge. If you are quiet it lets you.
plan.say: There is a grey cat that sits on the rail of the hoist loft, behind the forge. If you are quiet it lets you.

plan.speaker: ned
plan.text: Race you! No? Fine.
plan.say: Race you! No? Fine.

plan.speaker: ned
plan.text: I was not running.
plan.say: I was not running.

plan.speaker: fulk
plan.text: You get used to it. I did. Stand upwind, there, by the post.
plan.say: You get used to it. I did. Stand upwind, there, by the post.

plan.speaker: fulk
plan.text: Fulk Varrow. I turn hides into leather with bark, time and things you do not want named. Every boot in town began here.
plan.say: Fulk Varrow. I turn hides into leather with bark, time and things you do not want named. Every boot in town began here.

plan.speaker: fulk
plan.text: Humphrey Slate sells the meat and I get the hide. He gets the customers and I get the smell. We are still friends.
plan.say: Humphrey Slate sells the meat and I get the hide. He gets the customers and I get the smell. We are still friends.

plan.speaker: fulk
plan.text: Go along the lane where the washing hangs. People lose things there. People hide things there too.
plan.say: Go along the lane where the washing hangs. People lose things there. People hide things there too.

plan.speaker: fulk
plan.text: Upwind, upwind.
plan.say: Upwind, upwind.

plan.speaker: fulk
plan.text: Giles! The bark!
plan.say: Giles! The bark!

plan.speaker: fulk
plan.text: I know what water does to skin. I have a yard full of proof. That man had not been in the lake a day.
plan.say: I know what water does to skin. I have a yard full of proof. That man had not been in the lake a day.

plan.speaker: fulk
plan.text: Nobody comes here by day. So you are either lost or desperate. Which?
plan.say: Nobody comes here by day. So you are either lost or desperate. Which?

plan.speaker: giles
plan.text: I have washed. Twice. It does not come off, it only goes down a little.
plan.say: I have washed. Twice. It does not come off, it only goes down a little.

plan.speaker: giles
plan.text: Giles Varrow. One day I will be the tanner. I am trying to think of anything else I might be instead.
plan.say: Giles Varrow. One day I will be the tanner. I am trying to think of anything else I might be instead.

plan.speaker: giles
plan.text: Tilly Hobb sells bread by the bridge road. I buy a loaf a day. We do not need a loaf a day.
plan.say: Tilly Hobb sells bread by the bridge road. I buy a loaf a day. We do not need a loaf a day.

plan.speaker: giles
plan.text: Brandt is always short a pair of arms at the forge. If I were not bound here I would be asking him myself.
plan.say: Brant is always short a pair of arms at the forge. If I were not bound here I would be asking him myself.

plan.speaker: giles
plan.text: Does it show? The smell?
plan.say: Does it show? The smell?

plan.speaker: giles
plan.text: A loaf. Just the one.
plan.say: A loaf. Just the one.

plan.speaker: giles
plan.text: When the bell rang again I was at the pits. First thing in three weeks to sound better than this yard smells.
plan.say: When the bell rang again I was at the pits. First thing in three weeks to sound better than this yard smells.

plan.speaker: giles
plan.text: Father! ... He sleeps like the dead. Lucky for you. Go on, go.
plan.say: Father! ... He sleeps like the dead. Lucky for you. Go on, go.

plan.speaker: tybalt
plan.text: Smell that. Leather and beeswax. That is what my brother’s stink becomes once somebody with skill gets hold of it.
plan.say: Smell that. Leather and beeswax. That is what my brother's stink becomes once somebody with skill gets hold of it.

plan.speaker: tybalt
plan.text: Tybalt Varrow, saddler. Harness, girths, the Elder’s chair. Winifred stitches finer than I do and I say so.
plan.say: Tybalt Varrow, saddler. Harness, girths, the Elder's chair. Winifred stitches finer than I do and I say so.

plan.speaker: tybalt
plan.text: The wheelwright across the lane makes the cart and I make what pulls it. Miles Ashdown and I have never had a bad word, which is rare between neighbours.
plan.say: The wheelwright across the lane makes the cart and I make what pulls it. Miles Ashdown and I have never had a bad word, which is rare between neighbours.

plan.speaker: tybalt
plan.text: Edda’s plough harness is due for mending. If you are going to Fairweather Farm, tell her it is ready.
plan.say: Edda's plough harness is due for mending. If you are going to Fairweather Farm, tell her it is ready.

plan.speaker: tybalt
plan.text: Saddle soap. That is all it wants.
plan.say: Saddle soap. That is all it wants.

plan.speaker: tybalt
plan.text: Good hide, that. Fulk’s.
plan.say: Good hide, that. Fulk's.

plan.speaker: tybalt
plan.text: I made the straps for the bier. Hale wanted it done quiet. Nothing is quiet in a town of sixty.
plan.say: I made the straps for the bier. Hale wanted it done quiet. Nothing is quiet in a town of sixty.

plan.speaker: tybalt
plan.text: There is a child coming to this house in a month. I will not be gentle about who else comes into it.
plan.say: There is a child coming to this house in a month. I will not be gentle about who else comes into it.

plan.speaker: winifred
plan.text: Forgive me if I do not get up. I am stitching for two and sitting for two.
plan.say: Forgive me if I do not get up. I am stitching for two and sitting for two.

plan.speaker: winifred
plan.text: Winifred Varrow. I stitch the harness Tybalt cuts. Smaller hands, tighter seams.
plan.say: Winifred Varrow. I stitch the harness Tybalt cuts. Smaller hands, tighter seams.

plan.speaker: winifred
plan.text: Kat Ashdown leans on her gate at noon and I lean on mine, and between us nothing in Chapelgate goes unremarked.
plan.say: Kat Ashdown leans on her gate at noon and I lean on mine, and between us nothing in Chapelgate goes unremarked.

plan.speaker: winifred
plan.text: Maren has a tea she makes me. She is always short of what goes in it. She would be glad of someone who can climb.
plan.say: Marren has a tea she makes me. She is always short of what goes in it. She would be glad of someone who can climb.

plan.speaker: winifred
plan.text: Kat! Have you heard?
plan.say: Kat! Have you heard?

plan.speaker: winifred
plan.text: Not long now.
plan.say: Not long now.

plan.speaker: winifred
plan.text: I would like it all settled before the child comes. Tell me it is settled. Lie if you must.
plan.say: I would like it all settled before the child comes. Tell me it is settled. Lie if you must.

plan.speaker: winifred
plan.text: Tybalt. Do not get up angry. Get up slowly, and angry.
plan.say: Tybalt. Do not get up angry. Get up slowly, and angry.

plan.speaker: diggory
plan.text: Pots, pans, kettles, and whatever you have heard, I heard it first. What will it be?
plan.say: Pots, pans, kettles, and whatever you have heard, I heard it first. What will it be?

plan.speaker: diggory
plan.text: Diggory Pike. I mend what the smith is too proud to mend. A kettle is a small thing until it leaks.
plan.say: Diggory Pike. I mend what the smith is too proud to mend. A kettle is a small thing until it leaks.

plan.speaker: diggory
plan.text: Goda Malkin says Greta waters the ale. Greta says Goda brews in a boot. I sell to both and agree with whoever is nearer.
plan.say: Goda Malkin says Gretta waters the ale. Gretta says Goda brews in a boot. I sell to both and agree with whoever is nearer.

plan.speaker: diggory
plan.text: Somebody called the Magpie hides things about the town and leaves a note with each. I know three of the places. I will not say where. Look up, more often.
plan.say: Somebody called the Magpie hides things about the town and leaves a note with each. I know three of the places. I will not say where. Look up, more often.

plan.speaker: diggory
plan.text: Any pots to mend?
plan.say: Any pots to mend?

plan.speaker: diggory
plan.text: You did not hear it from me.
plan.say: You did not hear it from me.

plan.speaker: diggory
plan.text: A tally, silver in his teeth and a note for the Elder. I had all three before Hale had his helmet on.
plan.say: A tally, silver in his teeth and a note for the Elder. I had all three before Hale had his helmet on.

plan.speaker: diggory
plan.text: Alison, it is the one from the market! ... She says to tell you we have nothing but pans, and she has the heaviest.
plan.say: Alison, it is the one from the market! ... She says to tell you we have nothing but pans, and she has the heaviest.

plan.speaker: alison
plan.text: If he told you something, halve it. If he swore to it, halve it again.
plan.say: If he told you something, halve it. If he swore to it, halve it again.

plan.speaker: alison
plan.text: Alison Pike. He takes the stall and the talk. I do the mending that wants patience, here, in peace.
plan.say: Alison Pike. He takes the stall and the talk. I do the mending that wants patience, here, in peace.

plan.speaker: alison
plan.text: Goda’s small beer would strip tin. I buy a jug every evening. Do not look at me like that.
plan.say: Goda's small beer would strip tin. I buy a jug every evening. Do not look at me like that.

plan.speaker: alison
plan.text: Greta at the Hart is always after someone to run an errand. She pays in coin and a bed.
plan.say: Gretta at the Hart is always after someone to run an errand. She pays in coin and a bed.

plan.speaker: alison
plan.text: Halve it.
plan.say: Halve it.

plan.speaker: alison
plan.text: Evening. Jug’s empty.
plan.say: Evening. Jug's empty.

plan.speaker: alison
plan.text: Diggory has told that tale forty times and the man gets taller each time.
plan.say: Diggory has told that tale forty times and the man gets taller each time.
