plan.speaker: alison
plan.text: I have a skillet in each hand. Diggory, light the lamp so I can see which one to use.
plan.say: I have a skillet in each hand. Diggory, light the lamp so I can see which one to use.

plan.speaker: miles
plan.text: Mind the spokes, they are only wedged. Give me a moment, I have a felloe half on.
plan.say: Mind the spokes, they are only wedged. Give me a moment, I have a felloe half on.

plan.speaker: miles
plan.text: Miles Ashdown. Wheels, carts, barrows. If it rolls in Brackenfell I made it or I mended it.
plan.say: Miles Ashdown. Wheels, carts, barrows. If it rolls in Brackenfell I made it or I mended it.

plan.speaker: miles
plan.text: Brandt and I tyre the wheels together, him with the iron red and me with the water. Twenty years, and we have never cracked one.
plan.say: Brant and I tyre the wheels together, him with the iron red and me with the water. Twenty years, and we have never cracked one.

plan.speaker: miles
plan.text: The mill is east over the bridge and down the river. Osric owes me for a cart wheel; mention it and watch him go deaf.
plan.say: The mill is east over the bridge and down the river. Osric owes me for a cart wheel; mention it and watch him go deaf.

plan.speaker: miles
plan.text: Stand clear of the wheel.
plan.say: Stand clear of the wheel.

plan.speaker: miles
plan.text: True as a die, that one.
plan.say: True as a die, that one.

plan.speaker: miles
plan.text: I built the handcart they brought him up on. Made it for turnips.
plan.say: I built the handcart they brought him up on. Made it for turnips.

plan.speaker: miles
plan.text: I have a mallet that seats an oak spoke in one blow. Think it through.
plan.say: I have a mallet that seats an oak spoke in one blow. Think it through.

plan.speaker: kat
plan.text: He is working. Talk to me, I know what it costs and when it will be done, which he does not.
plan.say: He is working. Talk to me, I know what it costs and when it will be done, which he does not.
plan.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

plan.speaker: kat
plan.text: Kat Ashdown. He makes the wheels. I make them pay.
plan.say: Kat Ashdown. He makes the wheels. I make them pay.
plan.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

plan.speaker: kat
plan.text: Tamsin, Miles’s sister, lives two doors up with her bees. Twenty-seven, and writing letters to somebody. She will not say who.
plan.say: Tamsin, Miles's sister, lives two doors up with her bees. Twenty-seven, and writing letters to somebody. She will not say who.
plan.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

plan.speaker: kat
plan.text: Tamsin’s honey goes to the Hart. If you want to know why it is called the Honeyed Hart, taste the ale.
plan.say: Tamsin's honey goes to the Hart. If you want to know why it is called the Honeyed Hart, taste the ale.
plan.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

plan.speaker: kat
plan.text: Winifred! Noon!
plan.say: Winifred! Noon!
plan.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

plan.speaker: kat
plan.text: That will be two silver. Each.
plan.say: That will be two silver. Each.
plan.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

plan.speaker: kat
plan.text: Well. Nobody will call this a dull year. I had been hoping for a dull year.
plan.say: Well. Nobody will call this a dull year. I had been hoping for a dull year.
plan.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

plan.speaker: kat
plan.text: Miles, there is a thief. A poor one. He has come to a house full of wheels.
plan.say: Miles, there is a thief. A poor one. He has come to a house full of wheels.
plan.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

plan.speaker: tamsin
plan.text: Walk slowly and do not wave. They are in a good temper today and I would like it to last.
plan.say: Walk slowly and do not wave. They are in a good temper today and I would like it to last.

plan.speaker: tamsin
plan.text: Tamsin Ashdown. Eleven hives, and wax for the chandler. I prefer the bees to most company.
plan.say: Tamsin Ashdown. Eleven hives, and wax for the chandler. I prefer the bees to most company.

plan.speaker: tamsin
plan.text: The hunter, Wren. She brings me heather from the high slope for the hives. I write to thank her. Often.
plan.say: The hunter, Wren. She brings me heather from the high slope for the hives. I write to thank her. Often.

plan.speaker: tamsin
plan.text: There is a bee meadow east of the chapel, off the crag path. Go quietly and they will not mind you.
plan.say: There is a bee meadow east of the chapel, off the crag path. Go quietly and they will not mind you.

plan.speaker: tamsin
plan.text: Slowly. Slowly.
plan.say: Slowly. Slowly.

plan.speaker: tamsin
plan.text: Heather’s out on the tops.
plan.say: Heather's out on the tops.

plan.speaker: tamsin
plan.text: The bees were told. You have to tell them when someone dies or they leave. I did not know his name, so I said "a stranger".
plan.say: The bees were told. You have to tell them when someone dies or they leave. I did not know his name, so I said "a stranger".

plan.speaker: tamsin
plan.text: I keep bees, so I am not afraid of much. You have until I count to three, and I have already started.
plan.say: I keep bees, so I am not afraid of much. You have until I count to three, and I have already started.

plan.speaker: jasper
plan.text: Cord of ash, cord of oak. Ash for the forge, oak for the oven. What do you burn?
plan.say: Cord of ash, cord of oak. Ash for the forge, oak for the oven. What do you burn?

plan.speaker: jasper
plan.text: Jasper Holt. I keep the Hart, the forge and the bakehouse in fire. Without me this town is cold soup.
plan.say: Jasper Holt. I keep the Hart, the forge and the bakehouse in fire. Without me this town is cold soup.

plan.speaker: jasper
plan.text: Wren knows the woods better than I do and never lets me forget it. She is usually right, which is the worst of it.
plan.say: Wren knows the woods better than I do and never lets me forget it. She is usually right, which is the worst of it.

plan.speaker: jasper
plan.text: There is a lumber camp out on the forest road. A man called Hob worked it. He had a brother. Read the board at the old mine; do not ask me.
plan.say: There is a lumber camp out on the forest road. A man called Hob worked it. He had a brother. Read the board at the old mine; do not ask me.

plan.speaker: jasper
plan.text: Ash or oak?
plan.say: Ash or oak?

plan.speaker: jasper
plan.text: Dry wood! Seasoned!
plan.say: Dry wood! Seasoned!

plan.speaker: jasper
plan.text: I cut on every side of this town but one. North, under the cliffs, I leave standing. Now you know why.
plan.say: I cut on every side of this town but one. North, under the cliffs, I leave standing. Now you know why.

plan.speaker: jasper
plan.text: I split logs for a living. You are standing in my house. Work it out.
plan.say: I split logs for a living. You are standing in my house. Work it out.

plan.speaker: ysolt
plan.text: Mind the lines. If that sheet touches the ground I do it again, and I will know whose boot it was.
plan.say: Mind the lines. If that sheet touches the ground I do it again, and I will know whose boot it was.

plan.speaker: ysolt
plan.text: Ysolt Pell. I married into the name. It came with a house, a father-in-law at the door, and a hill nobody mentions.
plan.say: Ysolt Pell. I married into the name. It came with a house, a father-in-law at the door, and a hill nobody mentions.

plan.speaker: ysolt
plan.text: Brandt took my Tobin at the forge when no one else would have a Pell. The boy loses his hammer and Brandt roars, but he feeds him.
plan.say: Brant took my Tobbin at the forge when no one else would have a Pell. The boy loses his hammer and Brant roars, but he feeds him.

plan.speaker: ysolt
plan.text: I wash for the Hart. Greta always knows who wants a pair of hands, ask her.
plan.say: I wash for the Hart. Gretta always knows who wants a pair of hands, ask her.

plan.speaker: ysolt
plan.text: Off the lines!
plan.say: Off the lines!

plan.speaker: ysolt
plan.text: Dry by noon if the wind holds.
plan.say: Dry by noon if the wind holds.

plan.speaker: ysolt
plan.text: They say he wore a brass tally. Do not tell Lambert what number was on it. Let me be the one.
plan.say: They say he wore a brass tally. Do not tell Lambert what number was on it. Let me be the one.

plan.speaker: ysolt
plan.text: I have two boys and an old man asleep. Whatever you are after, it is not here, and I will scream the lane awake.
plan.say: I have two boys and an old man asleep. Whatever you are after, it is not here, and I will scream the lane awake.

plan.speaker: davy
plan.text: Have you seen a ewe with a torn ear? No. Nobody has. Warin will have my hide.
plan.say: Have you seen a ewe with a torn ear? No. Nobody has. Warin will have my hide.

plan.speaker: davy
plan.text: Davy Pell. I mind sheep for Warin Shaw. Ivo says the watch takes lads at sixteen. I am fifteen and three quarters.
plan.say: Davy Pell. I mind sheep for Warin Shaw. Eevo says the watch takes lads at sixteen. I am fifteen and three quarters.

plan.speaker: davy
plan.text: My brother Tobin is at the forge. He borrows things. He does not mean it as stealing, he means it as knights.
plan.say: My brother Tobbin is at the forge. He borrows things. He does not mean it as stealing, he means it as knights.

plan.speaker: davy
plan.text: There are outlaws camped up by the old tower, north of the chapel. Warin says they take lambs. I should like to see them try it with me there.
plan.say: There are outlaws camped up by the old tower, north of the chapel. Warin says they take lambs. I should like to see them try it with me there.

plan.speaker: davy
plan.text: Torn ear. Left one.
plan.say: Torn ear. Left one.

plan.speaker: davy
plan.text: Morning. Seen Warin?
plan.say: Morning. Seen Warin?

plan.speaker: davy
plan.text: Grandfather has not said a word since they brought the man up. He sits and he looks north.
plan.say: Grandfather has not said a word since they brought the man up. He sits and he looks north.

plan.speaker: davy
plan.text: Mother! ... I am nearly in the watch. Stand where you are.
plan.say: Mother! ... I am nearly in the watch. Stand where you are.

plan.speaker: lambert
plan.text: You will be wanting something. People only talk to a Pell when they want something.
plan.say: You will be wanting something. People only talk to a Pell when they want something.

plan.speaker: lambert
plan.text: Lambert Pell. I carried candles in the Old Mine when I was eleven. I came up one evening and Dunstan did not.
plan.say: Lambert Pell. I carried candles in the Old Mine when I was eleven. I came up one evening and Dunstan did not.

plan.speaker: lambert
plan.text: Rowan stood beside me the day they barred the door. Fifty years. He has never once said my brother’s name to me.
plan.say: Rowan stood beside me the day they barred the door. Fifty years. He has never once said my brother's name to me.

plan.speaker: lambert
plan.text: The mine is north-west, past the chapel and up under the cliffs. The Sexton kept the key. Ask the Brother what became of it.
plan.say: The mine is north-west, past the chapel and up under the cliffs. The Sexton kept the key. Ask the Brother what became of it.

plan.speaker: lambert
plan.text: North. Always look north.
plan.say: North. Always look north.

plan.speaker: lambert
plan.text: Hm. A stranger.
plan.say: Hm. A stranger.

plan.speaker: lambert
plan.text: I went down to the wharf. They would not lift the cloth for me. I did not need them to. I know my brother’s hands.
plan.say: I went down to the wharf. They would not lift the cloth for me. I did not need them to. I know my brother's hands.

plan.speaker: lambert
plan.text: Fifty years I have slept by this door waiting for a knock. You are not the one I was waiting for. Get out.
plan.say: Fifty years I have slept by this door waiting for a knock. You are not the one I was waiting for. Get out.

plan.speaker: warin
plan.text: You have caught me in the town, which is rare. The flock is on the west pasture with the lad.
plan.say: You have caught me in the town, which is rare. The flock is on the west pasture with the lad.

plan.speaker: warin
plan.text: Warin Shaw. Sheep, and a dog, and a house I use for sleeping. My niece married up to Highfold last month.
plan.say: Warin Shaw. Sheep, and a dog, and a house I use for sleeping. My niece married up to Highfold last month.

plan.speaker: warin
plan.text: Wren and I split the west slope between us. She takes what runs, I keep what grazes. We have never had a cross word.
plan.say: Wren and I split the west slope between us. She takes what runs, I keep what grazes. We have never had a cross word.

plan.speaker: warin
plan.text: There are outlaws camped on the passes and a notice on the board that pays for them. I would do it myself for a ewe apiece.
plan.say: There are outlaws camped on the passes and a notice on the board that pays for them. I would do it myself for a ewe apiece.

plan.speaker: warin
plan.text: Away to me. No, not you.
plan.say: Away to me. No, not you.

plan.speaker: warin
plan.text: Rain by evening.
plan.say: Rain by evening.

plan.speaker: warin
plan.text: I have pulled drowned sheep out of that lake. They are heavy. They say this one was light as a lamb.
plan.say: I have pulled drowned sheep out of that lake. They are heavy. They say this one was light as a lamb.

plan.speaker: warin
plan.text: The dog heard you at the gate. I let you get this far to see what you would do. Now go.
plan.say: The dog heard you at the gate. I let you get this far to see what you would do. Now go.

plan.speaker: ulric
plan.text: Walk beside me if you want to talk. The rope does not stop for conversation.
plan.say: Walk beside me if you want to talk. The rope does not stop for conversation.

plan.speaker: ulric
plan.text: Ulric Ferrin. Every rope in this town came off my walk. The well, the boats, the last bell rope, and the one before.
plan.say: Ulric Ferrin. Every rope in this town came off my walk. The well, the boats, the last bell rope, and the one before.

plan.speaker: ulric
plan.text: Brother Aldous sent to Marta Quill for his rope. Marta. A woman who sells buttons.
plan.say: Brother Aldous sent to Marta Quill for his rope. Marta. A woman who sells buttons.

plan.speaker: ulric
plan.text: The well rope is new this spring, mine, and sound. If you want to see what a rope should be, go and look at it.
plan.say: The well rope is new this spring, mine, and sound. If you want to see what a rope should be, go and look at it.

plan.speaker: ulric
plan.text: Mind the walk!
plan.say: Mind the walk!

plan.speaker: ulric
plan.text: Keep it taut, keep it taut.
plan.say: Keep it taut, keep it taut.

plan.speaker: ulric
plan.text: So the bell rings, on shop-bought hemp. Thirty feet. I would have laid forty and tarred the eye.
plan.say: So the bell rings, on shop-bought hemp. Thirty feet. I would have laid forty and tarred the eye.

plan.speaker: ulric
plan.text: I have a hundred fathoms of cord in this house and I can tie anything. Do not make me show you.
plan.say: I have a hundred fathoms of cord in this house and I can tie anything. Do not make me show you.

plan.speaker: beatrix
plan.text: Do not touch the green ones, they are not fired. Everything else you may pick up, if you buy what you drop.
plan.say: Do not touch the green ones, they are not fired. Everything else you may pick up, if you buy what you drop.

plan.speaker: beatrix
plan.text: Beatrix Ferrin. Ulric twists and I turn. Between us we make everything a house needs to hold and to hang.
plan.say: Beatrix Ferrin. Ulric twists and I turn. Between us we make everything a house needs to hold and to hang.

plan.speaker: beatrix
plan.text: Old Maren and I have traded jars for salves since before Amice was born. Her tonic is why I can still close my hands.
plan.say: Old Marren and I have traded jars for salves since before Amice was born. Her tonic is why I can still close my hands.

plan.speaker: beatrix
plan.text: Maren’s stores are thin and her knees are bad. If you are a walker, she will send you for herbs and pay in tonic.
plan.say: Marren's stores are thin and her knees are bad. If you are a walker, she will send you for herbs and pay in tonic.

plan.speaker: beatrix
plan.text: Careful. Careful!
plan.say: Careful. Careful!

plan.speaker: beatrix
plan.text: Kiln’s hot today.
plan.say: Kiln's hot today.

plan.speaker: beatrix
plan.text: Maren looked at him. She came here after and sat an hour by the kiln and did not say one word.
plan.say: Marren looked at him. She came here after and sat an hour by the kiln and did not say one word.

plan.speaker: beatrix
plan.text: Those shelves took me a month to fill. If one pot moves I will know it was you. Out.
plan.say: Those shelves took me a month to fill. If one pot moves I will know it was you. Out.

plan.speaker: amice
plan.text: Father says I talk too much to turn the wheel evenly. Hello.
plan.say: Father says I talk too much to turn the wheel evenly. Hello.

plan.speaker: amice
plan.text: Amice Ferrin. I turn the rope wheel and I am learning my letters from Master Sele.
plan.say: Amice Ferrin. I turn the rope wheel and I am learning my letters from Master Sele.

plan.speaker: amice
plan.text: Lettice has read every book on the stall. Twice. She told me how one ends and I have not forgiven her.
plan.say: Lettice has read every book on the stall. Twice. She told me how one ends and I have not forgiven her.

plan.speaker: amice
plan.text: If you stand on the terrace by the Elder’s, there is a glass you can look through. You can see the whole market.
plan.say: If you stand on the terrace by the Elder's, there is a glass you can look through. You can see the whole market.

plan.speaker: amice
plan.text: One, two, turn. One, two, turn.
plan.say: One, two, turn. One, two, turn.

plan.speaker: amice
plan.text: I was not listening!
plan.say: I was not listening!

plan.speaker: stephen
plan.text: Those have a week left in them. I can tell by how you stand. Sit down, let me look.
plan.say: Those have a week left in them. I can tell by how you stand. Sit down, let me look.

plan.speaker: stephen
plan.text: Stephen Alder. My father makes arrows; I wanted a trade where the customer comes back.
plan.say: Stephen Alder. My father makes arrows; I wanted a trade where the customer comes back.

plan.speaker: stephen
plan.text: Guardsman Ivo and I take a cup at the Hart most nights. He walks the wall and I mend what the wall does to his boots.
plan.say: Guardsman Eevo and I take a cup at the Hart most nights. He walks the wall and I mend what the wall does to his boots.

plan.speaker: stephen
plan.text: The wall walk is open if you want to see the town from above. Stair by the north houses. Mind the gap by the tower.
plan.say: The wall walk is open if you want to see the town from above. Stair by the north houses. Mind the gap by the tower.

plan.speaker: stephen
plan.text: Heels, friend. Look to your heels.
plan.say: Heels, friend. Look to your heels.

plan.speaker: stephen
plan.text: Evening, Ivo. Usual?
plan.say: Evening, Eevo. Usual?

plan.speaker: stephen
plan.text: He had miner’s boots. Old pattern, pegged, not sewn. Nobody has made that boot here since my grandfather.
plan.say: He had miner's boots. Old pattern, pegged, not sewn. Nobody has made that boot here since my grandfather.

plan.speaker: stephen
plan.text: I sleep over the shop for exactly this. That is an awl. It goes through ox hide.
plan.say: I sleep over the shop for exactly this. That is an awl. It goes through ox hide.

plan.speaker: emmet
plan.text: One moment. Amice, that is a b, not a d. Now. How may a man of letters disappoint you?
plan.say: One moment. Amice, that is a b, not a d. Now. How may a man of letters disappoint you?

plan.speaker: emmet
plan.text: Emmet Sele. I teach the children, write the letters, and keep the levy roll. I am the town’s memory and it treats me like its attic.
plan.say: Emmet Sele. I teach the children, write the letters, and keep the levy roll. I am the town's memory and it treats me like its attic.

plan.speaker: emmet
plan.text: Brother Aldous says the Sexton’s papers lie under the chapel in a hand he cannot read. I can. He has only to cross the square.
plan.say: Brother Aldous says the Sexton's papers lie under the chapel in a hand he cannot read. I can. He has only to cross the square.

plan.speaker: emmet
plan.text: The chapel has a crypt and the crypt has older books than mine. If you find the key, look at what the Sexton kept.
plan.say: The chapel has a crypt and the crypt has older books than mine. If you find the key, look at what the Sexton kept.

plan.speaker: emmet
plan.text: A b! A b!
plan.say: A b! A b!

plan.speaker: emmet
plan.text: Good day. Mind the ink.
plan.say: Good day. Mind the ink.

plan.speaker: emmet
plan.text: A brass tally with OM on it. The mine kept its own roll, and it went under the chapel with the Sexton’s things. Nobody has asked me about it. Nobody ever asks.
plan.say: A brass tally with OM on it. The mine kept its own roll, and it went under the chapel with the Sexton's things. Nobody has asked me about it. Nobody ever asks.

plan.speaker: emmet
plan.text: If you have come for the levy silver, it is not kept here. If you have come for a book, I am almost flattered. Leave.
plan.say: If you have come for the levy silver, it is not kept here. If you have come for a book, I am almost flattered. Leave.

plan.speaker: lettice
plan.text: You may read standing up for as long as you like. If you sit down, you have to buy it.
plan.say: You may read standing up for as long as you like. If you sit down, you have to buy it.

plan.speaker: lettice
plan.text: Lettice. Master Sele took me in when the carts lost my father on the pass. I keep his stall and correct his sums.
plan.say: Lettice. Master Sele took me in when the carts lost my father on the pass. I keep his stall and correct his sums.

plan.speaker: lettice
plan.text: Mistress Thorne brings her books back unread. She puts a ribbon at a different page each time. It is always a page with a picture.
plan.say: Mistress Thorne brings her books back unread. She puts a ribbon at a different page each time. It is always a page with a picture.

plan.speaker: lettice
plan.text: There are notes and letters all over this town if you look. People here write down what they will not say.
plan.say: There are notes and letters all over this town if you look. People here write down what they will not say.

plan.speaker: lettice
plan.text: That one ends sadly.
plan.say: That one ends sadly.

plan.speaker: lettice
plan.text: Do not bend it back!
plan.say: Do not bend it back!

plan.speaker: roger
plan.text: Look, do not thumb the edge. The last man who tested my work that way is still learning to write with his left.
plan.say: Look, do not thumb the edge. The last man who tested my work that way is still learning to write with his left.

plan.speaker: roger
plan.text: Roger Hask, cutler. Brandt makes the steel; I make it worth owning.
plan.say: Roger Hask, cutler. Brant makes the steel; I make it worth owning.

plan.speaker: roger
plan.text: Brandt Ironhand is the best smith on this side of the Greyspine and his knives are doorstops. I say it to his face.
plan.say: Brant Ironhand is the best smith on this side of the Greyspine and his knives are doorstops. I say it to his face.

plan.speaker: roger
plan.text: Brandt has lost his best hammer and half his temper. Find the one and you mend the other.
plan.say: Brant has lost his best hammer and half his temper. Find the one and you mend the other.

plan.speaker: roger
plan.text: Edge like a razor. Mind it.
plan.say: Edge like a razor. Mind it.

plan.speaker: roger
plan.text: Father! Slower on the wheel!
plan.say: Father! Slower on the wheel!

plan.speaker: roger
plan.text: Hale brought me the dead man’s knife to name the maker. No mark I know. Old iron, ground thin as a leaf.
plan.say: Hale brought me the dead man's knife to name the maker. No mark I know. Old iron, ground thin as a leaf.

plan.speaker: roger
plan.text: You walked into a cutler’s in the dark. Count your fingers on the way out.
plan.say: You walked into a cutler's in the dark. Count your fingers on the way out.

plan.speaker: odo
plan.text: Who is that? Come where the light is. No use, is it. Speak, then, I know a voice.
plan.say: Who is that? Come where the light is. No use, is it. Speak, then, I know a voice.

plan.speaker: odo
plan.text: Odo Hask. Seventy-nine. I was a grown man when Rowan was a boy, and you may tell him I said so.
plan.say: Odo Hask. Seventy-nine. I was a grown man when Rowan was a boy, and you may tell him I said so.

plan.speaker: odo
plan.text: Idony Hobb and I are the last two who heard the hill when it sang. She will not talk of it. I will, if you ask me.
plan.say: Idony Hobb and I are the last two who heard the hill when it sang. She will not talk of it. I will, if you ask me.

plan.speaker: odo
plan.text: Look at the east wall of the Hart’s cellar. There is brick in it younger than I am. I never drank there after.
plan.say: Look at the east wall of the Hart's cellar. There is brick in it younger than I am. I never drank there after.

plan.speaker: odo
plan.text: Who is that?
plan.say: Who is that?

plan.speaker: odo
plan.text: Good steel sings. Listen.
plan.say: Good steel sings. Listen.

plan.speaker: odo
plan.text: There. Hear it? I count my days by that bell. Three weeks I did not know if I was dead.
plan.say: There. Hear it? I count my days by that bell. Three weeks I did not know if I was dead.

plan.speaker: odo
plan.text: I am blind, not deaf. Third board from the door. You are standing on it.
plan.say: I am blind, not deaf. Third board from the door. You are standing on it.

plan.speaker: randal
plan.text: Do not lean on her. She is green wood and steam and she is still deciding what shape to be.
plan.say: Do not lean on her. She is green wood and steam and she is still deciding what shape to be.

plan.speaker: randal
plan.text: Randal Byrd. I build boats. My brother makes barrels, which are boats that gave up.
plan.say: Randal Byrd. I build boats. My brother makes barrels, which are boats that gave up.

plan.speaker: randal
plan.text: Old Wenn taught me everything and still tells me I plank like a farmer. I would not trade him for a new shed.
plan.say: Old Wenn taught me everything and still tells me I plank like a farmer. I would not trade him for a new shed.

plan.speaker: randal
plan.text: Finn Reedwater is at the end of the dock from first light. He found the man. He will tell it, if you ask kindly.
plan.say: Finn Reedwater is at the end of the dock from first light. He found the man. He will tell it, if you ask kindly.

plan.speaker: randal
plan.text: Mind the strakes.
plan.say: Mind the strakes.

plan.speaker: randal
plan.text: Fair wind on the lake.
plan.say: Fair wind on the lake.

plan.speaker: randal
plan.text: They sent for me to look at the wharf. No boat brought that man. No keel mark, no oar. He walked out of the water.
plan.say: They sent for me to look at the wharf. No boat brought that man. No keel mark, no oar. He walked out of the water.

plan.speaker: randal
plan.text: The tar pot is still warm. I would rather not waste it on you.
plan.say: The tar pot is still warm. I would rather not waste it on you.

plan.speaker: wenn
plan.text: Twenty boats. There were twenty on this water when I had my hair. Now sit down, I am going to tell you about each one.
plan.say: Twenty boats. There were twenty on this water when I had my hair. Now sit down, I am going to tell you about each one.

plan.speaker: wenn
plan.text: Wenn. Just Wenn. I built boats for sixty years and now I hold the keys and the opinions.
plan.say: Wenn. Just Wenn. I built boats for sixty years and now I hold the keys and the opinions.

plan.speaker: wenn
plan.text: Randal is the best pupil I ever had and I will tell him so on my deathbed and not one hour before.
plan.say: Randal is the best pupil I ever had and I will tell him so on my deathbed and not one hour before.

plan.speaker: wenn
plan.text: The keys to the boat-houses are with me, and there they stay. Read the board on the wharf if you want to know how high the lake once stood.
plan.say: The keys to the boat-houses are with me, and there they stay. Read the board on the wharf if you want to know how high the lake once stood.

plan.speaker: wenn
plan.text: Twenty boats!
plan.say: Twenty boats!

plan.speaker: wenn
plan.text: Planks like a farmer.
plan.say: Planks like a farmer.

plan.speaker: wenn
plan.text: I have seen what Mirrormere gives back. It gives back the drowned. That one, it did not want.
plan.say: I have seen what Mirror meer gives back. It gives back the drowned. That one, it did not want.

plan.speaker: wenn
plan.text: Eh? Is it morning? No. Then you are a thief, and I am too old to chase you. Shut the door on your way out.
plan.say: Eh? Is it morning? No. Then you are a thief, and I am too old to chase you. Shut the door on your way out.

plan.speaker: barnaby
plan.text: Candles, cord, tar, tallow and lamp oil. Light and rope: there is nothing else a person truly needs.
plan.say: Candles, cord, tar, tallow and lamp oil. Light and rope: there is nothing else a person truly needs.

plan.speaker: barnaby
plan.text: Barnaby Crane, chandler. Tamsin’s wax, Ulric’s cord, my wicks.
plan.say: Barnaby Crane, chandler. Tamsin's wax, Ulric's cord, my wicks.

plan.speaker: barnaby
plan.text: Ursel says I should have asked the Elder which cave. Ursel says a good many things after the event.
plan.say: Ursel says I should have asked the Elder which cave. Ursel says a good many things after the event.

plan.speaker: barnaby
plan.text: The gate is short of lamp oil and there is a notice for it. Marta Quill has the flasks.
plan.say: The gate is short of lamp oil and there is a notice for it. Marta Quill has the flasks.

plan.speaker: barnaby
plan.text: Tallow or wax?
plan.say: Tallow or wax?

plan.speaker: barnaby
plan.text: Long evenings coming. Stock up.
plan.say: Long evenings coming. Stock up.

plan.speaker: barnaby
plan.text: The Elder bought a dozen candles off me every month, "for the cave". I took it for a manner of speaking.
plan.say: The Elder bought a dozen candles off me every month, "for the cave". I took it for a manner of speaking.

plan.speaker: barnaby
plan.text: I can lay my hand on a candle in the dark faster than you can find the door. Shall we see?
plan.say: I can lay my hand on a candle in the dark faster than you can find the door. Shall we see?

plan.speaker: ursel
plan.text: He will tell you light and rope are all a person needs. Ask him who cooks.
plan.say: He will tell you light and rope are all a person needs. Ask him who cooks.

plan.speaker: ursel
plan.text: Ursel Crane. I keep the counter. I also ask the questions, since somebody must.
plan.say: Ursel Crane. I keep the counter. I also ask the questions, since somebody must.

plan.speaker: ursel
plan.text: Mercy Garrick sweeps the widow’s step across the way, every week, a house nobody has lived in for years. Ask yourself why.
plan.say: Mercy Garrick sweeps the widow's step across the way, every week, a house nobody has lived in for years. Ask yourself why.

plan.speaker: ursel
plan.text: Widow Hale’s house is locked and has been since she died. Somebody has the key. It is not the Warden; I asked.
plan.say: Widow Hale's house is locked and has been since she died. Somebody has the key. It is not the Warden; I asked.

plan.speaker: ursel
plan.text: Which cave, though?
plan.say: Which cave, though?

plan.speaker: ursel
plan.text: Mind the tar.
plan.say: Mind the tar.

plan.speaker: ursel
plan.text: A dozen candles a month for a cave, and my husband never once said "which cave, Elder?" Thirty years I have been married to that.
plan.say: A dozen candles a month for a cave, and my husband never once said "which cave, Elder?" Thirty years I have been married to that.

plan.speaker: ursel
plan.text: Barnaby. Light a candle. We have enough of them. I want to see this person’s face.
plan.say: Barnaby. Light a candle. We have enough of them. I want to see this person's face.

plan.speaker: silas
plan.text: Hm. ... Stone does not talk either. It is why I like it.
plan.say: Hm. ... Stone does not talk either. It is why I like it.

plan.speaker: silas
plan.text: Garrow. Mason. Walls, hearths, and every stone in the churchyard since my father’s.
plan.say: Garrow. Mason. Walls, hearths, and every stone in the churchyard since my father's.

plan.speaker: silas
plan.text: Finn and I drink at the same table at the Hart and say nothing. It suits us both.
plan.say: Finn and I drink at the same table at the Hart and say nothing. It suits us both.

plan.speaker: silas
plan.text: The north wall has a stair and a walk. I built the steps. From the top you can see the old tower on its crag.
plan.say: The north wall has a stair and a walk. I built the steps. From the top you can see the old tower on its crag.

plan.speaker: silas
plan.text: Hm.
plan.say: Hm.

plan.speaker: silas
plan.text: Good stone, that.
plan.say: Good stone, that.

plan.speaker: silas
plan.text: The Brother has asked me for a headstone and given me no name to cut. I have left it blank. It will not be the first.
plan.say: The Brother has asked me for a headstone and given me no name to cut. I have left it blank. It will not be the first.

plan.speaker: silas
plan.text: I lift stone for a living. Go.
plan.say: I lift stone for a living. Go.

plan.speaker: humphrey
plan.text: Mutton, pork when there is pork, and sausage you should not ask about. What will you have?
plan.say: Mutton, pork when there is pork, and sausage you should not ask about. What will you have?

plan.speaker: humphrey
plan.text: Humphrey Slate, butcher. Edda’s beasts, Warin’s sheep, my knife. Hester keeps the till so there is some left.
plan.say: Humphrey Slate, butcher. Edda's beasts, Warin's sheep, my knife. Hester keeps the till so there is some left.

plan.speaker: humphrey
plan.text: Hale has had three words with me about blood in the lane. Where does he think meat comes from? A tree?
plan.say: Hale has had three words with me about blood in the lane. Where does he think meat comes from? A tree?

plan.speaker: humphrey
plan.text: The watch pays for outlaws put down on the passes. I would go myself, but who would cut the chops?
plan.say: The watch pays for outlaws put down on the passes. I would go myself, but who would cut the chops?

plan.speaker: humphrey
plan.text: Fresh today! Mostly!
plan.say: Fresh today! Mostly!

plan.speaker: humphrey
plan.text: Do not ask about the sausage.
plan.say: Do not ask about the sausage.

plan.speaker: humphrey
plan.text: I helped carry him. I have carried sides of beef that were more alive. Dry, he was. Dry as jerky.
plan.say: I helped carry him. I have carried sides of beef that were more alive. Dry, he was. Dry as jerky.

plan.speaker: humphrey
plan.text: Hester! Cleaver! ... No, I have it. Friend, I joint a hog in the time it takes you to reach that door.
plan.say: Hester! Cleaver! ... No, I have it. Friend, I joint a hog in the time it takes you to reach that door.

plan.speaker: hester
plan.text: He shouts. He always shouts. The meat is good and the weights are honest, that is what matters.
plan.say: He shouts. He always shouts. The meat is good and the weights are honest, that is what matters.
plan.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

plan.speaker: hester
plan.text: Hester Slate. I keep the block clean and the till closed.
plan.say: Hester Slate. I keep the block clean and the till closed.
plan.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

plan.speaker: hester
plan.text: Avice Hobb and I were girls together. She married bread and I married meat, and we meet in the middle every market day.
plan.say: Avice Hobb and I were girls together. She married bread and I married meat, and we meet in the middle every market day.
plan.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

plan.speaker: hester
plan.text: Ellen Marsh smokes fish down by the water. If you want lake trout, hers is the best.
plan.say: Ellen Marsh smokes fish down by the water. If you want lake trout, hers is the best.
plan.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

plan.speaker: hester
plan.text: Honest weight, every time.
plan.say: Honest weight, every time.
plan.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

plan.speaker: hester
plan.text: Avice! A word!
plan.say: Avice! A word!
plan.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

plan.speaker: hester
plan.text: I saw them bring him up the lane. I have told Avice and nobody else, and Avice has told the town.
plan.say: I saw them bring him up the lane. I have told Avice and nobody else, and Avice has told the town.
plan.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

plan.speaker: hester
plan.text: Humphrey has the cleaver. I have the other cleaver. There are always two.
plan.say: Humphrey has the cleaver. I have the other cleaver. There are always two.
plan.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

plan.speaker: goda
plan.text: The bush is out, so the beer is ready. A farthing a jug and it will not put honey on your tongue or airs in your head.
plan.say: The bush is out, so the beer is ready. A farthing a jug and it will not put honey on your tongue or airs in your head.

plan.speaker: goda
plan.text: Goda Malkin. I brew for people who work. Greta brews for people who sit.
plan.say: Goda Malkin. I brew for people who work. Gretta brews for people who sit.

plan.speaker: goda
plan.text: Greta Barleybrook and I have not had a civil word in ten years and I would trust her with my last penny.
plan.say: Gretta Barleybrook and I have not had a civil word in ten years and I would trust her with my last penny.

plan.speaker: goda
plan.text: Osric at the mill owes half the town malt. If you are passing, tell him Goda remembers, and Greta is first in the line.
plan.say: Osric at the mill owes half the town malt. If you are passing, tell him Goda remembers, and Gretta is first in the line.

plan.speaker: goda
plan.text: Bush is out!
plan.say: Bush is out!

plan.speaker: goda
plan.text: Farthing a jug.
plan.say: Farthing a jug.

plan.speaker: goda
plan.text: Rings like it never stopped. I will say this for the Hart: Greta sent a cask round the night it came back, for everyone.
plan.say: Rings like it never stopped. I will say this for the Hart: Gretta sent a cask round the night it came back, for everyone.

plan.speaker: goda
plan.text: Bridget! The mash paddle! ... It is six feet of oak, stranger. I stir with it daily.
plan.say: Bridget! The mash paddle! ... It is six feet of oak, stranger. I stir with it daily.

plan.speaker: bridget
plan.text: Mother will tell you Greta’s ale is honey and airs. I drink at the Hart on Fridays. Do not tell her.
plan.say: Mother will tell you Gretta's ale is honey and airs. I drink at the Hart on Fridays. Do not tell her.

plan.speaker: bridget
plan.text: Bridget Malkin. I do the brewing now, mostly. Mother does the selling and the feud.
plan.say: Bridget Malkin. I do the brewing now, mostly. Mother does the selling and the feud.

plan.speaker: bridget
plan.text: The tailor, Jocelyn. He measures me with his eyes every time I pass. I could do worse. I am checking whether I could do better.
plan.say: The tailor, Jocelyn. He measures me with his eyes every time I pass. I could do worse. I am checking whether I could do better.

plan.speaker: bridget
plan.text: Lark plays at the Hart every evening. He says he knows nine songs and seven of them are sad. Ask him for one.
plan.say: Lark plays at the Hart every evening. He says he knows nine songs and seven of them are sad. Ask him for one.

plan.speaker: bridget
plan.text: Small beer, fresh.
plan.say: Small beer, fresh.

plan.speaker: bridget
plan.text: Friday. Do not tell her.
plan.say: Friday. Do not tell her.

plan.speaker: bridget
plan.text: People want beer when things change and beer when they do not. It is a steady trade, at least.
plan.say: People want beer when things change and beer when they do not. It is a steady trade, at least.

plan.speaker: bridget
plan.text: Mother, do not get up, I have it. You. Out, before she finds the paddle.
plan.say: Mother, do not get up, I have it. You. Out, before she finds the paddle.

plan.speaker: adda
plan.text: Rush for seats, willow for carrying. Do not sit on the willow.
plan.say: Rush for seats, willow for carrying. Do not sit on the willow.

plan.speaker: adda
plan.text: Adda. They call me the Rushworker. I cut my own reeds on the north shore and I have the hands to prove it.
plan.say: Adda. They call me the Rushworker. I cut my own reeds on the north shore and I have the hands to prove it.

plan.speaker: adda
plan.text: My brother lives up by the fall, by himself. People say hermit and mean mad. He is neither. He is tired of people, which is sense.
plan.say: My brother lives up by the fall, by himself. People say hermit and mean mad. He is neither. He is tired of people, which is sense.

plan.speaker: adda
plan.text: Follow the stream up past the old tower and you come to a pool under a fall. If a man is there, let him be. He is my brother, and he is not mad.
plan.say: Follow the stream up past the old tower and you come to a pool under a fall. If a man is there, let him be. He is my brother, and he is not mad.

plan.speaker: adda
plan.text: Rushes, fresh cut.
plan.say: Rushes, fresh cut.

plan.speaker: adda
plan.text: Not on the willow!
plan.say: Not on the willow!

plan.speaker: adda
plan.text: A man comes out of the dark alone and they cover him with a sail. My brother went into the hills alone. I think of it.
plan.say: A man comes out of the dark alone and they cover him with a sail. My brother went into the hills alone. I think of it.

plan.speaker: adda
plan.text: I weave by touch, so I do not need the lamp to find you. Out you go.
plan.say: I weave by touch, so I do not need the lamp to find you. Out you go.

plan.speaker: peter
plan.text: The boat is not for hire today, the caulking is wet. And I do not go to the west shore, wet or dry.
plan.say: The boat is not for hire today, the caulking is wet. And I do not go to the west shore, wet or dry.

plan.speaker: peter
plan.text: Peter Marsh. I row what needs rowing. My father did, his father did. Marsh House has always had oars by the door.
plan.say: Peter Marsh. I row what needs rowing. My father did, his father did. Marsh House has always had oars by the door.

plan.speaker: peter
plan.text: Finn Reedwater is on that dock before I am up and after I am in. I do not know when the man sleeps.
plan.say: Finn Reedwater is on that dock before I am up and after I am in. I do not know when the man sleeps.

plan.speaker: peter
plan.text: West shore, past the reeds, there is a cleft in the rock by the water. I have seen a light in it before dawn. I rowed the other way.
plan.say: West shore, past the reeds, there is a cleft in the rock by the water. I have seen a light in it before dawn. I rowed the other way.

plan.speaker: peter
plan.text: Penny across.
plan.say: Penny across.

plan.speaker: peter
plan.text: Not the west shore.
plan.say: Not the west shore.

plan.speaker: peter
plan.text: Finn found him. Everyone says so. Finn found him. That is right.
plan.say: Finn found him. Everyone says so. Finn found him. That is right.

plan.speaker: peter
plan.text: Ellen, take Will upstairs. ... I have an oar. I know it is a foolish thing to hold indoors. I am holding it.
plan.say: Ellen, take Will upstairs. ... I have an oar. I know it is a foolish thing to hold indoors. I am holding it.

plan.speaker: ellen
plan.text: Mind the rack, it is hot. Trout and eel, done over alder. Here at the door, if you ask nicely.
plan.say: Mind the rack, it is hot. Trout and eel, done over alder. Here at the door, if you ask nicely.

plan.speaker: ellen
plan.text: Ellen Marsh. He catches the fares, I catch the supper.
plan.say: Ellen Marsh. He catches the fares, I catch the supper.

plan.speaker: ellen
plan.text: Mercy Garrick mends our nets and will not take full price. Her brother is on the passes with the outlaws; she pays for him in knots.
plan.say: Mercy Garrick mends our nets and will not take full price. Her brother is on the passes with the outlaws; she pays for him in knots.

plan.speaker: ellen
plan.text: Peter knows every yard of the lake shore. Ask him about the west side and watch him find something to do with his hands.
plan.say: Peter knows every yard of the lake shore. Ask him about the west side and watch him find something to do with his hands.

plan.speaker: ellen
plan.text: Smoked trout!
plan.say: Smoked trout!

plan.speaker: ellen
plan.text: Will! Off the dock!
plan.say: Will! Off the dock!

plan.speaker: ellen
plan.text: Peter came home grey that morning, before anyone had cried the news. He says he saw nothing. I have been married eleven years.
plan.say: Peter came home grey that morning, before anyone had cried the news. He says he saw nothing. I have been married eleven years.

plan.speaker: ellen
plan.text: Peter. Wake up. Take the oar. Yes, the oar.
plan.say: Peter. Wake up. Take the oar. Yes, the oar.

plan.speaker: will
plan.text: Finn says I am not to talk when the float is moving. Is the float moving? I am not allowed to look.
plan.say: Finn says I am not to talk when the float is moving. Is the float moving? I am not allowed to look.

plan.speaker: will
plan.text: I am Will. I am eight. I can row if someone else holds one of the oars.
plan.say: I am Will. I am eight. I can row if someone else holds one of the oars.

plan.speaker: will
plan.text: Finn caught a pike as long as me. He let me carry the tail end.
plan.say: Finn caught a pike as long as me. He let me carry the tail end.

plan.speaker: will
plan.text: There is a dead man under a sail on the wharf. I am not allowed to look at that either.
plan.say: There is a dead man under a sail on the wharf. I am not allowed to look at that either.

plan.speaker: will
plan.text: Is it moving?
plan.say: Is it moving?

plan.speaker: will
plan.text: I did not touch it!
plan.say: I did not touch it!

plan.speaker: mercy
plan.text: Talk if you like. I can mend and listen. I cannot mend and be looked at.
plan.say: Talk if you like. I can mend and listen. I cannot mend and be looked at.

plan.speaker: mercy
plan.text: Mercy Garrick. Yes. That Garrick. He was a good boy and a bad man, and I knew him as both.
plan.say: Mercy Garrick. Yes. That Garrick. He was a good boy and a bad man, and I knew him as both.

plan.speaker: mercy
plan.text: The widow Hale was kind to me when this whole lane was not. So I sweep her step. I do not need a better reason.
plan.say: The widow Hale was kind to me when this whole lane was not. So I sweep her step. I do not need a better reason.

plan.speaker: mercy
plan.text: There is a notice at the Hart that pays for outlaws. I will not ask you not to. I will ask you to tell me, after, if one of them had one ear.
plan.say: There is a notice at the Hart that pays for outlaws. I will not ask you not to. I will ask you to tell me, after, if one of them had one ear.

plan.speaker: mercy
plan.text: Mind the nets.
plan.say: Mind the nets.

plan.speaker: mercy
plan.text: Knots hold. People do not.
plan.say: Knots hold. People do not.

plan.speaker: mercy
plan.text: The roads will be safer or they will not. Either way there is a man out there with one ear who is still my brother.
plan.say: The roads will be safer or they will not. Either way there is a man out there with one ear who is still my brother.

plan.speaker: mercy
plan.text: I leave a light in that window for someone and it is not you. Out.
plan.say: I leave a light in that window for someone and it is not you. Out.

plan.speaker: alaric
plan.text: Good day. Humours out of balance, I can see it from here. A touch choleric. I have a tincture.
plan.say: Good day. Humours out of balance, I can see it from here. A touch choleric. I have a tincture.

plan.speaker: alaric
plan.text: Alaric Mossop, apothecary, late of the lowland towns. Two years here. They still call me the new man.
plan.say: Alaric Mossop, apothecary, late of the lowland towns. Two years here. They still call me the new man.

plan.speaker: alaric
plan.text: Old Maren sells weeds in a twist of rag and half the town swears by her. I have glass jars. I have labels.
plan.say: Old Marren sells weeds in a twist of rag and half the town swears by her. I have glass jars. I have labels.

plan.speaker: alaric
plan.text: The woman Maren sends people up the slopes for frostcaps and pays them in tonic. I call that hedge-craft. You may call it what you like.
plan.say: The woman Marren sends people up the slopes for frostcaps and pays them in tonic. I call that hedge-craft. You may call it what you like.

plan.speaker: alaric
plan.text: Choleric. Decidedly.
plan.say: Choleric. Decidedly.

plan.speaker: alaric
plan.text: I have a tincture for that.
plan.say: I have a tincture for that.

plan.speaker: alaric
plan.text: Dry lungs, they tell me, and the herb-woman is "reading" him. Reading. I offered a proper examination. I was not answered.
plan.say: Dry lungs, they tell me, and the herb-woman is "reading" him. Reading. I offered a proper examination. I was not answered.
